Quick Answer
macOS 27 Golden Gate has far more useful features than the ones you will notice immediately after updating. I tested more than 27 of them and picked the 27 worth trying, including Siri AI, custom Safari extensions, smarter Shortcuts, new Photos tools, and several smaller additions. Go through this list, and you will likely find a few features that can make the way you use your Mac easier.
Apple has finally released macOS 27 Golden Gate, and unlike the last few macOS updates, this one feels like a much bigger update. Apple has changed how macOS looks, added the new Siri AI, brought several Apple Intelligence features to its built-in apps, and made noticeable changes to Safari, Photos, Notes, Calendar, and many other places that you will notice once you start using your Mac.
I have been using macOS 27 and trying these features on my Mac, and some of them are genuinely useful. Some of my favorites is the new Siri that does many more things than previous, also Safari that lets you create your own extension simply by describing what you want it to do.
There are plenty of smaller additions like this throughout macOS 27. Some solve problems I have had with macOS for a long time, while others add things that previously required a third-party app or a much longer workaround. In this article, I will show you the best macOS 27 Golden Gate features I have found so far, what has changed, and how you can try them on your Mac.
Table of Contents
27 Best macOS 27 Golden Gate Features
macOS 27 Golden Gate comes with countless new features and small changes, and covering every single one of them in one article isn’t possible. After digging deeper into the update and trying many of these features myself, I have picked the best 27 that I found the most useful and that I think most Mac users should know about. Some are easy to notice, while others are hidden inside the apps and settings you already use every day.
Talk With Siri AI and Continue Your Previous Conversations
Siri has received one of its biggest changes on the Mac with macOS 27. Instead of only appearing as the small Siri interface we have been using for years, Siri AI now has its own app where you can start a conversation, ask follow-up questions, and return to your previous conversations later.
This is particularly useful when I have already given Siri all the context about something, and whenever needed, I can reopen that conversation instead of explaining everything again.
To use the Siri AI app on your Mac, first make sure Siri is enabled.
Once it is enabled, open the Siri app, where you will find all your previous conversations in the left sidebar and the chat window on the right. You can select any previous conversation to continue chatting or start a new conversation with Siri. If you right-click on any conversation in the sidebar, you will also see additional options to pin or delete the conversation.
Search Your Mac and Ask Siri Directly From Spotlight
Spotlight is one of the features I use almost every day on my Mac. With macOS 27, it also becomes a quick way to access Siri AI, so I don’t have to open the dedicated Siri app whenever I have a small question.
You just have to press Command + Space to open Spotlight and continue typing normally when you want to find an app, file, document, or setting. When you want to ask Siri AI something instead, just type your query normally and hit return to get an answer. You can also access whatever you have searched in Spotlight in the dedicated Siri app as a separate conversation.
I prefer using this for quick questions and keeping the Siri app for longer conversations where I know I will need follow-up questions.
Create Your Own Safari Extension Just by Describing It
Safari already supports extensions, but I still have to find an extension that does exactly what I need. With macOS 27, I can simply describe the functionality I want, and Safari can create an extension for me using Apple Intelligence.
I tried this with Instagram. I sometimes watch Reels on Instagram’s website, but it doesn’t give me a playback bar to quickly move forward or backward in a Reel. Instead of searching for an extension, I asked Safari to create one using this prompt:
Prompt: Create an extension for Instagram that adds playback controls to Reels and lets me move forward or backwards in the video while watching a Reel.
Surprisingly, it worked. After enabling the generated extension, I could seek forward and backwards while watching Instagram Reels. If there is a small website-specific feature you have always wanted, this gives you a way to try building it yourself.
To create one:
- Open Safari on your Mac and visit the website for which you want to create an extension.
- Click on the Page menu inside Safari’s address bar and select Describe Extension.
- Describe exactly what you want the extension to do. “I recommend keeping the request focused on one particular problem instead of asking it to change several unrelated things on the website.”
- Safari will first check whether an existing extension from the App Store can do what you described. If you don’t want one of the suggested extensions, click Create to generate your own.
- Once Safari creates the extension, click Try and test it on the website. Don’t save it immediately; use the website normally for a few minutes and make sure the extension actually behaves the way you expected.
- If something isn’t working correctly, click Edit and describe what you want Safari to change. Once you are happy with the result, click Save to keep the extension.
If you are new to browser extensions, you can check our list of the best Safari extensions for Mac to see what else extensions can add to Safari.
Create Shortcuts by Simply Explaining What You Want
Shortcuts can automate plenty of repetitive tasks on a Mac, but creating a complicated shortcut manually isn’t always easy. macOS 27 lets you describe what you want in normal language, and Apple Intelligence can put together the required Shortcut actions for you.
For example, I created a simple shortcut for work. Whenever I start working, I need to open TechPP, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress. Instead of opening each website manually, I created a shortcut that opens all four websites in Chrome whenever I run it.
Prompt: Create a shortcut that opens techpp.com, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress in Chrome.
Here’s how you can create it:
- Open the Shortcuts app on your Mac and click the plus (+) button.
- Enter the prompt in the Describe a shortcut field and let Apple Intelligence create the shortcut for you.
- Once it is created, click Run or the Play icon to test it.
Use Visual Intelligence to Understand What’s on Your Screen
Visual Intelligence on the Mac works differently from the camera-based experience on the iPhone. In macOS 27, I can select something already visible on my screen and ask Siri AI about it, which is useful when the thing I am looking at is easier to show than describe.
Suppose I see a chair in an image and want to know what kind of chair it is or find similar designs. Instead of describing its shape, material, and appearance, I can press Command + Shift + 6, select the chair on the screen, and choose Ask Siri to ask about it. There is also an Image Search option when I want to find visually similar results online.
Adjust How Much Liquid Glass You Want on Your Mac
Apple introduced Liquid Glass across its operating systems last year, but macOS 27 now gives you more control over how transparent the interface actually looks. Instead of having to accept one fixed appearance, there is now a slider that lets you choose how clear or tinted you want Liquid Glass to be.
To adjust it:
- Open the System Settings on your Mac and click Appearance in the sidebar.
- Find the Liquid Glass adjustment inside the Appearance settings.
- Move the slider toward the left if you want the interface to look clearer and more transparent. Move it toward the right if you want more tint and less of the background showing through.
Hide Extra Menu Bar Icons and Access Them When You Need Them
My Mac’s menu bar gets crowded quickly because several utilities I use throughout the day add their own icons. macOS 27 handles this better with a new overflow control that hides icons when there isn’t enough space and gives you a double-arrow button to reveal them whenever you need them. This means I don’t have to remove a useful menu bar utility just because I don’t need its icon visible every minute. This is especially useful on MacBooks with a notch, where menu bar space is already limited.
Let Safari Automatically Organise Your Tabs Into Topics
I am terrible at keeping my browser tabs under control, particularly when I am researching something and have several unrelated pages open at the same time. Safari already has Tab Groups on Mac, which are useful when you manually organize related tabs. macOS 27 takes this a step further by using Apple Intelligence to automatically identify related tabs and organize them into topics. Each topic gets a label and a tab count, and you can collapse a topic when you aren’t working on it without actually closing those tabs.
For example, while researching for this article, I might have 10–15 tabs open about different macOS features, along with a few Amazon shopping tabs and some work-related pages. Instead of showing all of them together in one long row, Safari can automatically identify which tabs are related and organise them into separate topics such as macOS 27, Shopping, and Work. I can keep the macOS 27 topic expanded while I am researching and collapse Shopping and Work to hide those tabs temporarily. Whenever I need them again, I can simply expand that topic without having to search through all my open tabs.
To enable it:
- Open Safari on your Mac and click Safari in the menu bar at the top left of the screen.
- Choose Settings, and then switch to Tabs section.
- Then click the drop-down menu right to Organise tabs and select Automatically Create Topics.
- Continue browsing normally and open a few pages related to the same subject. Safari will identify related tabs and place them under a topic when it recognises the connection.
Change the Perspective of a Photo With Reframe
Cropping can remove unnecessary space from a photo, but it can’t change the angle from which the photo appears to have been taken. The new Reframe feature goes further by using Apple Intelligence to change the perspective and angle of an existing image.
I find this useful when I like a photo but wish I had taken it from a slightly different angle or positioned the subject differently. To use it:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo.
- Click the Edit button in the top-right corner to open the photo editing tools.
- Click Tools and select Reframe from the available options.
- Drag the photo or use the available perspective controls to change how you want the final image to be framed. I recommend making smaller adjustments first instead of immediately trying to create a completely different camera angle.
- Once you have the angle you want, click Reframe and wait for Apple Intelligence to generate the additional parts required for the new perspective.
- Pay particular attention to faces, hands, and other objects whose shape is easy to recognize. If everything looks right, Finally click Save Changes.
Expand a Photo Beyond Its Original Frame With Extend
There have been times when I had a good portrait photo but couldn’t use it as a wallpaper or inside a presentation because converting it to a wider aspect ratio would crop an important part of the image, and where the new Extend feature comes in. It generate additional content outside the original frame with Apple Intelligence.
To try it, open the image in Photos, click Edit, and open Tools. Select Extend, drag the edges beyond the original photo or choose the aspect ratio you need, and click Extend to generate the missing area.
Check the newly generated areas carefully before saving the result. If you don’t like what it created, adjust the frame and try again instead of keeping an obviously generated section.
Remove Unwanted Objects From Photos With Clean Up
Apple introduced the Clean Up tool with Apple Intelligence, and macOS 27 improves how it handles larger unwanted objects. If I take a photo at a tourist spot and someone is standing in the background I can select that person and let Photos remove them.
Here’s how you can remove an unwanted object from a photo:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo you want to edit.
- Click Edit in the upper-right corner and open Tools.
- Select Clean Up, and your Mac will analyse the image. In some cases, Photos may automatically highlight objects it thinks you might want to remove.
- Click on a highlighted object to remove it, or use the Erase brush to paint over the object yourself. You can also circle the object if that makes it easier to select.
- And, finally, click Clean Up.
Resize the iPhone Mirroring Window
iPhone Mirroring is useful when I want to access something on my iPhone without picking it up, but using everything inside a phone-sized window on a large Mac display isn’t always ideal. macOS 27 fixes this by letting you resize the iPhone Mirroring window just by dragging its corner. You can also use keyboard shortcuts to quickly resize the iPhone Mirroring window. Press Command + Plus (+) to increase the window size and Command + Minus (-) to decrease it. If you want to return the window to its default size, press Command + 0.
But macOS 27 takes resizing a step further with supported apps. When you open a resizable app and make the iPhone Mirroring window wider, the app can actually adjust its layout and show more content instead of simply making the same iPhone interface bigger.
For example, if I open a supported app and drag the iPhone Mirroring window into a wider layout, I can get more usable screen space and information inside the app. Not every app supports this yet, so in unsupported apps, resizing may simply make the existing interface larger or smaller. You can press Command + 9 whenever you want to return the window to the standard iPhone size.
Let Your Mac Suggest Better Names for Files and Folders
My Downloads folder has taught me how quickly bad filenames can become a problem. A name such as “Untitled” or “Document 2” becomes useless once I forget what is inside them.
With macOS 27, Apple Intelligence can suggest names for files and folders based on what they contain. Instead of having to open a document again just to remember what it was about, macOS can look at the content and suggest a name that actually describes it.
First, you have to make sure this feature is enabled on your Mac. To do so, open Finder and click the Finder button in the menu bar. Next, choose Settings and make sure you are in the General tab. Now, check the box next to Suggest Filenames.
Now, to use this feature, right-click any document, photo, screenshot, or folder in Finder and select Rename. Wait for around five seconds, and Finder will show you a few suggested names based on the file’s contents. You can select the name you like and use it instead of typing one manually.
Create and Edit Calendar Events by Describing Them
macOS 27 makes creating Calendar events faster by describing the event naturally instead of filling in every field separately. I can type something like “Pankaj’s birthday next Monday,” and Calendar can use those details to create the event.
To try it, open Calendar, click the plus (+) button, and enter your description in Describe Event. You can also describe changes to an existing event instead of manually changing individual details.
Draw Directly Inside Apple Notes on Your Mac
Not everything you want to save in a note needs to be written as text. For example, if you’re planning the layout of a room, sketching a quick idea, making a simple diagram, or noting down something that is easier to remember visually, a quick drawing can be more useful than typing it out. With macOS 27, you can now create these drawings directly inside a note on your Mac and keep them saved along with the rest of your notes.
Previously, you could create drawings in a note from an iPhone or iPad, but macOS didn’t let you draw directly inside Notes on the Mac. Now, you can use your mouse or trackpad to create a quick sketch without leaving the Notes app.
Here’s how you can draw inside a note:
- Open the Notes app.
- Click the Markup button in the Notes toolbar to open the drawing tools.
- Choose the drawing tool you want to use, and adjust its thickness and colour depending on what you are trying to draw.
- Start drawing directly inside the note using your mouse or trackpad.
- Once you are finished, click the Markup button again to exit the drawing tools and continue working on the rest of your note.
Generate Images in More Styles With Image Playground
I tested Image Playground on Mac when Apple first introduced it, and one of my biggest complaints was how limited the available styles felt. Now, Apple has made Image Playground much more flexible in macOS 27. You now get more styles, including create photorealistic images, and the Any Style option lets you describe the kind of visual appearance you want instead of choosing only from a small set of presets. You can also choose square, portrait, or landscape output depending on where you plan to use the image.
Another change I find more useful is targeted editing. If most of the generated image looks good but there is one part I want to change, I can select that area and describe the change instead of generating the entire image again and hoping everything else remains the same.
If you are using Image Playground for the first time, I recommend reading our complete Image Playground guide for Mac, where we have covered the interface, creating images, using your own photos, and managing generated images in more detail.
Record Your Mac Screen With System Audio
This is one of my favorite smaller additions in macOS 27, especially because I regularly work on tutorials. macOS has had a built-in screen recorder for a long time, but recording the sound coming directly from the Mac hasn’t been nearly as straightforward as recording the screen itself.
The difference between system audio and microphone audio is important here. If I am recording a tutorial and an app plays a sound, system audio captures that sound directly. I don’t have to turn up my MacBook speakers and let the microphone record them along with keyboard sounds, fan noise, and everything else happening in the room.
Here’s how you can record your Mac screen with system audio:
- Press Shift + Command + 5 on your keyboard to open the built-in screenshot and screen-recording toolbar.
- Choose whether you want to Record Entire Screen, Record Selected Portion, or Selected Window depending on what you want to capture.
- Click Options in the toolbar and enable Include System Audio so that sounds playing on your Mac are included in the recording.
Add Extra-Large Widgets to Your Mac Desktop
I have been using widgets on my Mac desktop since Apple introduced them with macOS Sonoma. but the existing widget sizes don’t always work when an app has more information to show.
macOS 27 adds new Extra Large widget sizes, including a portrait layout for supported widgets. The additional space lets apps show considerably more information on the desktop.
To add an extra large widget on your desktop:
- Right-click anywhere on your Mac desktop and select Edit Widgets.
- Find the app whose widget you want to add and look through the available widget sizes. If the app supports the new sizes, you should see Extra Large or Extra Large Portrait among the options.
- Select the size you want and add the widget to your desktop.
If you haven’t used desktop widgets before, we have a complete guide explaining how to add widgets to your Mac desktop, including how to customise the widgets already on your Mac.
Share Photos and Videos in Full Resolution With Shared Albums
Shared Albums are convenient when I want to collect photos from a trip, event, or family function in one place, but there has always been a compromise: the photos and videos shared through them weren’t necessarily kept in their original quality.
Apple changes that with the new Shared Albums experience in macOS 27. Newly created permanent Shared Albums can store photos and videos at full resolution
Let Android and Windows Users Add Photos to Your Shared Albums
The Shared Albums update gets even more useful if your friends or family don’t all use Apple devices. Previously, you needed several WhatsApp chats, Google Drive folders, and people sending pictures individually
With macOS 27, people on Android and Windows can access the updated Shared Albums through a web browser, and they don’t necessarily need an Apple Account to participate. More importantly, you can allow them to contribute photos instead of limiting them to viewing the album.
Save Any Frame From a Video Directly as a Photo
Sometimes the best photo from a moment is actually hidden inside a video. Before macOS 27, if we spotted an interesting moment in a video, the easiest way to save it as a photo was to take a screenshot. But a screenshot doesn’t preserve the video frame as cleanly as a dedicated photo, and you may end up with lower quality or unwanted elements from the screen. With macOS 27, you can now save any video frame directly as a separate photo in your Photos library.
Open the video in Photos, pause it at the moment you want, and check the nearby frames until you find the best one. Then right-click the frame and select Save Video Frame as Photo. The saved frame appears in your Photos library, where you can edit and share it just like any other photo.
Start a Slideshow Directly From a Photo Album
I usually organise photos from a trip or event into an album, but when I want to show those pictures to someone, opening them one by one isn’t the nicest way to do it. macOS 27 makes this easier by letting me start a slideshow directly from an album in Photos, so I can show the entire collection without having to open every photo individually.
Slideshows themselves aren’t new on the Mac, but I like that I can now start one directly from an album I have already organised. Once the slideshow starts, I can quickly customise how it plays by changing the transition and duration, adding music, and deciding whether it should loop.
Here’s how you can start a slideshow from an album:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and find the album you want to show.
- Control-click the album and select Start Slideshow from the menu.
- Once the slideshow starts, click Customise if you want to change how it plays.
- Adjust the Transition & Duration settings to control how quickly the photos move from one to another, and choose music if you want something playing in the background.
Change How Fast and Expressive Siri Sounds
I don’t always want Siri to speak at the same pace. If I am following instructions, a slightly slower response can be easier to understand. And if the current voice feels too slow, you can make it speak faster. macOS 27 also lets you change more than just how fast Siri speaks. On supported Macs and voices, you can also adjust how expressive the voice sounds. Increasing this setting gives Siri’s speech more variation and emphasis, which can make the spoken responses feel more natural and animated.
Get Better Resolution Support for External Displays
macOS 27 improves external display support, including 5K at 120Hz on certain compatible ultrawide monitors. Apple has also improved how macOS restores window positions and display arrangements after disconnecting and reconnecting a monitor, which I find more useful when regularly docking and undocking a MacBook.
After connecting your monitor, open System Settings, select Displays, and choose the external monitor to see the available resolutions and refresh rates.
Make Buttons and Other Controls Easier to See With Show Borders
macOS 27 adds a new Show Borders accessibility option that makes the boundaries around buttons and other interface controls easier to distinguish. This can be useful if you don’t want some controls to blend into the background with the Liquid Glass design.
To enable it, open System Settings and click Accessibility in the left sidebar. Select Display from the right-side panel, find Show Borders, and turn on the toggle next to it. You can also try Reduce Transparency from the same section if transparency itself is making parts of the interface difficult to see.
Explore Cities With More Detailed 3D Views in Apple Maps
Apple has improved the 3D city experience in Maps with more detailed buildings and surroundings in supported locations. I don’t use 3D Maps every time I need directions, but it can be useful when I want to understand the layout of an unfamiliar area before visiting it.
To try it, open Maps and search for the city or location you want to explore. Click View in the menu bar, select Show 3D Map, and enable Satellite if you want to explore the area using the detailed imagery.
Try the New Golden Gate Wallpapers and Screen Savers
Finally, macOS 27 comes with new Sunset and Night views of the Golden Gate Bridge, along with a new abstract wallpaper. The Golden Gate scenes can also be used as screen savers.
To try them, open System Settings and select Wallpaper from the left sidebar. Browse through the new macOS 27 backgrounds and select the one you want to use.
macOS 27 Feels More Useful Once You Start Finding the Smaller Changes
After trying more than 27 new macOS 27 features, creating custom Safari extensions is still the one I enjoyed the most, while several smaller additions have also made my everyday Mac experience better. If you enjoyed this guide, also check out our 27 best iOS 27 features you should try on your iPhone.
FAQs about macOS 27
1. Do All macOS 27 Features Work on Every Mac That Supports macOS 27?
No. Your Mac may support macOS 27 but still miss some features because individual features can have additional hardware, language, or region requirements.
2. Can Safari Extensions I Create Be Shared With Other People?
Not directly. Safari’s Describe Extension feature creates custom extensions for your own use. You can sync compatible extensions across your own Apple devices, but Apple currently doesn’t provide an option to send a generated extension directly to another person.
3. Can I Downgrade to macOS 26 After Installing macOS 27?
Yes, as long as macOS 26 supports your Mac. However, downgrading isn’t available like a normal software update and may require erasing your Mac and reinstalling the older macOS version. So, make sure you have a complete backup before proceeding.

Saka responds to Arteta's challenge with 'huge impact'
- Published
Bukayo Saka responded to the challenge set by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as he proved a game-changer in the 3-0 Champions League win over Lille.
The England forward has been told he should aim to score "two or three" goals per game - such was his quality and the expectation from his boss.
Saka did not achieve that tally against the French visitors, but shook off illness to come off the bench and assist Eberechi Eze's strike that made it 2-0, before rolling in his side's third goal.
The 25-year-old has now scored four goals in nine games this season and looks to be taking the next step in his evolution as Arsenal's key man.
With the majority of his side's attacking play involving him, he has always been an influential figure. But with opposition defenders doubling up on him and injury issues over the last two seasons, there were doubts over whether Saka could still do what was asked of him in attack or if he had lost a yard of pace.
Arteta has tweaked Saka's positioning this season and, prior to Lille's visit, said it has been done deliberately to get him closer to the goal.
'He delivered with real quality'
"That is where we need to get him," said the Gunners boss before the game. "And if he misses the chance, so be it. At the end, the more volume we generate, the bigger the probability of him scoring more goals."
Saka's strike against Lille was a confident one-touch finish and came after he missed a late one-on-one opportunity in Saturday's Premier League victory over Leeds.
"He has been getting in great positions, getting shots, getting one-touch finishes and tap-ins," added Arteta.
"That is the kind of unpredictability we have with that player, otherwise we know how the opponent is going to defend him. He is doing well, he could have had another four or five goals by now, easily. But if he continues like that, we know.
"When he talks about scoring a certain amount of goals, he needs to be thinking about scoring a certain amount of goals per game. If that shifts, that mentality, he will get into those positions and score more goals."
Saka has scored 20 goals in a season just once in his career, which came in the 2023-24 campaign and 16 in the Premier League.
But the winger has also been in good goalscoring form for England with five in his last four matches and scored a double in the 7-0 Nations League demolition of Croatia in the recent international break.
Saka is now on 19 goals in major European competitions for Arsenal, only behind Thierry Henry (42), while he has nine assists in the Champions League which puts him behind Henry (16) and Cesc Fabregas (14).
He has refused to disclose the targets he has set himself, but Arteta welcomed Saka's response following his message to do more in front of goal.
The Spaniard said: "I don't know if that's the case, but I am very happy.
"He wasn't feeling that good yesterday and today, as he had some sort of illness. He wasn't ready to start but he was really wanting to contribute to the team if it was needed and he came on and made a huge impact and delivered with real quality."
Arteta revealed he also spoke to Saka after telling the media about his desire for the player to have a greater impact.
"After the press conference... I said 'Bukayo, I just killed you in the press conference, good luck tomorrow'.
"He was laughing. He knows that we have discussed these kind of things and he takes it because he wants to be the best version of himself.
"In order to do that, you have to put big objectives and challenges and try to reason by working and being consistent - and when it doesn't work, keep going because he has the ability to do it."
Gyokeres struggles on mixed night for fringe players
Arteta made five changes to the team that started the win over Leeds as the Gunners looked to navigate six matches in all competitions during this month.
Noni Madueke moved to the right wing after putting in a good performance on the left at the weekend, with Mikel Merino, Eze and Viktor Gyokeres all coming into the starting XI.
Eze had started just two games in all competitions before the match with Lille and Arteta had said his attitude had been "phenomenal" despite a lack of game time.
The 28-year-old showed flashes of his undoubted quality and his finish for Arsenal's second goal - and his first of the season - will give him confidence going forward.
Madueke had a mixed night as he showed his ability to beat a defender, but questions remain over his end product - even if he provided the assist for Jurrien Timber's classy opening goal.
However, it was not a good night for Gyokeres.
The Sweden striker scored 21 goals in all competitions last season as Arsenal won the title for the first time in 22 years and displayed his willingness to run and work hard.
But Gyokeres had just 12 touches before being replaced and Kai Havertz, as he so often does, looked a much better and more natural fit for the Arsenal frontline, teeing up Saka's goal too.
Arteta brought on Saka, Havertz and Martin Odegaard after going 1-0 up and all three contributed to show why they are still the first names on the teamsheet and why the Arsenal boss will be so reliant on them if they are to achieve more honours.

For years, Chinese hardware manufacturers have carved out a market niche with an array of handheld Android gaming devices focused on retro emulation and/or more modern game-streaming capabilities. Now, though, a major game industry trade group is targeting one of those manufacturers, Anbernic, asking the US Trade Representative (USTR) to add the company to its list of “Notorious Markets” that “engage in or facilitate substantial copyright piracy or trademark counterfeiting.”
TorrentFreak was among the first to notice the request from the Entertainment Software Association (ESA), which was submitted to the USTR last week. In it, the US trade group—which represents major publishers including Nintendo, Microsoft, PlayStation, Amazon, Epic, EA, Ubisoft, and more—notes that Anbernic devices “are routinely offered or shipped with removable memory cards preloaded with hundreds or thousands of unauthorized copies of copyright-protected video games published by ESA members.”
While many online sellers do include an SD card full of ROMs alongside emulation hardware of all types, Anbernic itself does not appear to do the same when selling directly from its website. Regardless, the ESA argues that these ROM-laden Anbernic devices selling through “normal retail channels” help to “normalize hardware-based piracy by delivering illicit catalogues through a polished consumer product.” This, the ESA says, meets the threshold for a “superfake,” an ill-defined designation that applies to “high-quality counterfeit trademark goods … on a commercial scale.”
Being included on the USTR’s Notorious Market List wouldn’t bring any additional direct legal consequences for a company like Anbernic. However, the USTR says the list “encourages the responsible authorities to step up efforts to combat piracy and counterfeiting” and notes that the list itself “increase[s] public awareness and help market operators and governments prioritize intellectual property enforcement efforts that protect American businesses and their workers.” Inclusion on the list could also presage a Section 301 investigation that could lead to legal consequences or restrictive import controls on the devices.

Pope Leo XIV under went successful surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung on Tuesday after an examination confirmed he had lung cancer.
Tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin after the surgery. It said the diagnosis had been suspected based on preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery.
“The operation was successful, and there were no complications,” the Holy See Press Office said.
The Vatican said doctors were not currently considering chemotherapy or other therapies pending the results of further tests. The Vatican press office noted that the medical statement's reference to the “radical” removal of the lobe indicated that doctors had removed all suspected tissue in the hope of eliminating any remaining traces of the cancer.
The surgery took place at Rome's Gemelli Hospital and lasted around 90 minutes, according to the Holy See Press Office. The Pope spent approximately three hours in the operating room.
Doctors used a video-assisted surgical technique to remove the affected portion of the lung. An examination of the tissue during the procedure confirmed the diagnosis, which had been suspected based on preoperative tests.
Pope Leo awoke normally after the operation and returned to his room on the hospital's 10th floor following a brief period of observation, Vatican News reported.
The surgical team was led by Professor Stefano Margaritora, assisted by Professor Elisa Meacci, Dr Maria Teresa Congedo and Dr Leonardo Petracca Ciavarella. Professor Massimo Antonelli, Dr Giovanni Punzo and Dr Giuseppe Bello were part of the anaesthesia team.
Further tests on the removed tissue are expected in the coming days. Doctors had conducted preoperative examinations to establish the location of the affected tissue and plan the procedure.
The Vatican has not announced any change to the Pope's expected hospital stay of one week.
Following the surgery, Pope Leo asked for dinner and spent the evening with his secretaries and other Vatican staff, Matteo Bruni, director of the Holy See Press Office, said, according to Vatican News.
The Agostino Gemelli Polyclinic Hospital in Rome is a major medical centre that has treated several popes over the years.

‘I never imagined that eight months…’

"I never imagined that eight months of my hard work would go to waste like this," Bittu wrote in the caption.
He also asked social media users to suggest ways to remove more garbage from the Ajnar River efficiently.

Meet India's feisty Gen Z protester who is taking on Modi
- Published
When India's Gen Z-led protesters return to Delhi this weekend for demonstrations seeking the resignation of the country's top election official, one of the prominent faces at the forefront will be that of a 29-year-old PhD student.
Neha Bora is a theatre artist and activist who has been with the All India Students' Association (Aisa), a Left-wing organisation known for campus politics, for the past decade and been its president for the past two years.
But Neha's - who uses "they" and "them" as personal pronouns - visibility is no longer limited to campuses.
Viral videos over the past few days show them being dragged through the street by a group of female police officials, climbing on top of police barricades, raising their fist and shouting slogans, and being detained.
Photos of them smiling while being carried away by policewomen have also gone viral.
In a recent BBC Bangla interview, Neha played down the attention they've been receiving.
"I know it happened in front of the camera so it seems like it's something different," they said. "But I have seen all student activists with the Left doing the same things that I have been doing. It's just that there is a camera on me, so people think something different is happening."
The attention on Neha comes at a time when several high-profile protests are being held on India's streets in what is being seen as one of the biggest challenges to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 12 years in power.
There's the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) - a Gen Z-led online satirical movement - that held weeks-long protests in Delhi in the summer over education reforms. It ended in July only after education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
Separately, some of India's opposition parties, especially the Congress, have also taken to the streets over electoral reforms. For the past few days, videos of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra being shoved and jostled and detained have gone viral and made headlines in India.
Saturday's protest in Delhi has been called by the CJP, which is seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating electoral rolls to favour Modi's BJP. Both the Election Commission and the BJP have rejected the accusation.
Although not a member of the CJP, Neha has said their group would also participate.
Born in the northern state of Uttarakhand, Neha lived in different cities as a child as their army officer father moved for his postings.
After graduating from Delhi University, they did a master's degree from Ambedkar University in the capital and are now a PhD student at the prestigious Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).
Neha first came into the spotlight in the summer during the CJP's protest over education reforms.
Neha and Aisa were at the protest from the start, but not many knew them at that point. That changed after 28 June, when educationist and scientist Sonam Wangchuk began a hunger strike in CJP's support and Neha and a few others from Aisa also joined him.
"It was an obvious choice for us. We've been protesting against paper leaks and education reforms for a long time," Neha later said in an interview.
While most of the attention was focused on Wangchuk, whose reputation and presence galvanised the movement, Neha's outspokenness and combative speeches began to get them noticed.
After Wangchuk and others were moved to hospital, Neha continued fasting despite having lost 8kg.
Even after being moved to hospital, they said in a video: "The fight continues. Once I've recovered, we'll meet you again on the streets to continue our fight for our right."
After the protests ended in July, Neha has established themselves as a Gen Z leader who's courted by the CJP and media, besides appearing alongside Rahul Gandhi at press conferences.
But Neha's involvement with Aisa and leftist politics and statements criticising PM Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and other BJP leaders have also led to "lots of disagreements with my family as my parents are staunch supporters of BJP".
And last month, at least three police complaints were lodged, external in Uttar Pradesh state by BJP against Neha for making "objectionable remarks" against the chief minister - they came two days after Aisa's police complaint that Neha had received death threats, external.
Neha, who has been travelling to many Indian cities to participate in protests in support of students, also made headlines when a man allegedly threw ink, external at them during a protest march in Jharkhand state. A photo Neha shared on Instagram showed their face streaked with ink stains. Police said they had detained the man.
The noisy protests and repeated detentions have earned Neha a reputation for being a street fighter.
"The streets have always dictated the course of politics in this country and they will continue to do so, more so in the coming few years," they told BBC Bangla.
"If we look at the social changes of the recent past, those social changes did not come from people sitting in parliament; they came from the streets," they said.
Now as the authorities gear up for 10 October's protest at Jantar Mantar against CEC Kumar, Neha and Aisa have said they would be back in the streets with the CJP to "protect democracy".

- To start the An Unheard Farewell quest in Valor Mortis, players have to talk to the Adjutant Sous-Officier in the Valley of Ashes.
- The quest requires players to find the scout, who is located on the mid-level of the elevator in that area.
- Defeat the tainted mini-boss, secure the letter, and brief the officer to complete this quest.
Valor Mortis has some really interesting side quests, and one of the first ones you get in the game is called An Unheard Farewell. Like other soulslike games, the side quests in Valor Mortis can also be a bit cryptic. Many players are already having trouble with the very first side quest. So, here is a complete guide to Valor Mortis ‘An Unheard Farewell’ quest.
How to Start Valor Mortis ‘An Unheard Farewell’ Quest
To start the An Unheard Farewell quest in Valor Mortis, players will need to make their way into the Valley of Ashes. This place unlocks after fighting General Lothaire for the first time. Once in the Valley of Ashes, make your way to the next Lantern location. Once you reach there, you will find a carriage with a voice coming from inside.
This voice belongs to an Adjutant Sous-Officier, who asks you to find the scouts he sent out. If you agree to help, the An Unheard Farewell quest will begin for you.
How to Complete Valor Mortis ‘An Unheard Farewell’ Quest
The quest is fairly straightforward. All you have to do is find the missing scout’s location and defeat him to obtain the letter. Now, the issue is that the quest diverges from the main questline in the game. So, it can become difficult for players to find the scout’s location. So, here is how you can complete the Valor Mortis ‘An Unheard Farewell’ quest:
- Go down to the carriage from the Lantern, where you will find the Pistol.
- At the very bottom, you will find another lantern. Walk along the pier and jump to the spot above.
- Shoot at the red blob at a distance to destroy it. Learn how to destroy red blob in Valor Mortis from our guide if you have any doubts.
- Now, the lift will become available for use. Jump on it and wait for it to reach the first level. When the lift becomes stuck, jump to the right side and use the fire magic to burn the barrier.
- Enter the cave and make your way up until you exit. Continue going forward until you reach the top of the elevator.
- When you reach the elevator, destroy the two red blobs on each side to remove the corruption. Now call up the elevator and use it to get back down.
- While going down, look for a new platform on the left and jump to it. Burn the blocked path there and go inside the cave.
- Inside, you will find the missing scout, who will be a mini-boss. Defeat him and read the letter on the table near the ladder.
- Now, return to the Adjutant Sous-Officier to brief him about the details. This will complete the quest.
Valor Mortis ‘An Unheard Farewell’ Quest Reward
After completing the Valor Mortis ‘An Unheard Farewell’ quest, you will get the Sleight of Hand Amber. This Amber gives the following passive effect when slotted into the Skill Tree:
- Sleight of Hand: Reduces the reload times for Firearms and speeds up weapon switching.
That’s the only reward you get for completing this quest. However, there are some chests along the way that can provide some additional items.
So, that’s it. Now you know how to complete the An Unheard Farewell quest in Valor Mortis. If you have any questions, ask us in the comments below.

Tamil Nadu has achieved the National AIDS Control Programme-Phase V (NACP-V) target of 95-95-95 during 2026-27 under which 95% of people living with HIV know their status, 95% of those diagnosed are on antiretroviral therapy (ART) and 95% of those receiving treatment achieve viral suppression, Health Minister K.G. Arunraj said on Monday.
Officials said the State achieved the target in September this year. The Minister, while participating in an event on a State-level intensified IEC campaign on HIV/AIDS, said the prevalence of HIV/AIDS was down by half in the State; it has dropped from 0.40% in 2010 to 0.19% in 2023 as a result of sustained and intensive awareness efforts by the State government and NGOs.
The aim, he said, was to increase awareness and achieve a HIV/AIDS-free Tamil Nadu by 2030. Currently, 1,63,151 people are under treatment in the State, he added. He said a total of 311 integrated counselling and testing centres (ICTC) functioned in the State with funding support from the National AIDS Control Organisation, while 403 ICTCs functioned through financial assistance from the National Health Mission. A total of 2,656 testing facilities functioned at primary health centres and government hospitals, a press release said.
Free HIV testing
Free testing for HIV, prevention, and treatment services are provided through ART centres in 58 government health facilities, including government medical college hospitals, district headquarters hospitals, and government hospitals, and 28 ART centres in private medical colleges hospitals and 172 linked ART centres. As many as 104 NGOs and social organisations have been working to bring about behavioural changes among high risk groups in the State. This includes sex workers, men who have sex with men, people who inject drugs, transpersons, heavy vehicle drivers, and migrants, he added.
The Minister said eliminating mother-to-child transmission of three infections — HIV, Syphilis, and Hepatitis B — was another key priority. Babies born to HIV-positive women were given a prophylactic dose of ART soon after birth to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HIV, he added.
Taking into consideration the need to provide social protection for children living with HIV/AIDS through nutritious food, uninterrupted education, and continuous treatment, the State government enhanced the monthly financial assistance provided to children affected by HIV/AIDS.
The revised monthly assistance was ₹3,000 for children living with HIV who have lost both parents, ₹2,000 for children who have lost one parent, ₹1,500 for children who live with their parents, and ₹1,500 for children who have lost both parents to HIV/AIDS but are not infected. An additional ₹1.21 crore has been allocated for this scheme and the enhanced assistance will benefit children from November onward, the Minister said.
He said the intensified awareness campaign on HIV/AIDS must reach every section of the society. Through the Tamil Nadu State AIDS Control Society (TANSACS), Red Ribbon Clubs have been set up in 2,329 colleges to create awareness among students about HIV/AIDS, sexually transmitted infections, and behavioural change. To create awareness on HIV/AIDS prevention among adolescents, life skills education training is being imparted to students studying in classes VIII, IX, and XI in 9,830 schools through the State Council of Educational Research and Training, Dr. Arunraj added.
Health Secretary Darez Ahamed and Project Director of TANSACS R. Seethalakshmi were present.

The TOI correspondent from Washington:
 US President Donald Trump insists Russia and China are not doing much to help Iran in its war with America and Israel. “If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all,” the MAGA supremo declared on Monday, arguing that Moscow and Beijing had too much to lose by getting involved.
The assessment is not universally shared by American pundits who have pointed to Russian intelligence assistance to Tehran and Chinese-linked supplies of technology and components that could sustain Iran’s military capabilities. Yet Trump appears determined not to let such doubts obstruct his relationship with either leader, ties now on display with his puzzling call to buy Russian diesel and his decision to attend an APEC meeting in Shenzhen in November where he will meet Xi for a second time in two months, to likely be followed by a third in December at the G-20 meet in Florida.
In a move that has infuriated Ukraine, unsettled European allies, mystified India, and prompted bipartisan protests in Washington, Trump has agreed to open the American market to Russian fuel -- in itself remarkable for someone who brags incessantly about the U.S being energy surplus -- while easing sanctions imposed to punish Moscow for invading Ukraine. The ostensible reason is soaring diesel prices ahead of midterm elections on Nov 3, with Trump needing to show that he can bring down the cost of living to forestall a rout.
The electoral calculation is straightforward: Diesel is the lifeblood of trucking, agriculture, construction and much of the goods-distribution economy and high prices raise operating costs for farmers and truckers, feeding into consumer prices to provide Democrats with an obvious line of attack against a president who promised manna. Small problem: the transaction is so insignificant -- the initial shipment would cover less than a day's demand in the U.S and the first three announced tranches would amount to only a few days' consumption -- that analysts are looking for hidden agenda in the deal.
While Russia stands to earn hundreds of millions of dollars from the initial shipments, the broader waiver provides Moscow with an opportunity to resume exports and challenge the principle that its energy revenues should be restricted while its war against Ukraine continues -- the argument Washington made while bearing down on India.
Trump, predictably, has doubled down on the two-timing. On Monday he invoked the European Union's past purchases of Russian energy, claiming the bloc had paid Russia $250 billion, without specifying the period covered. His argument is essentially that Washington should not be held to a stricter standard than European capitals, hypocrisy from both sides (U.S and Europe) that New Delhi called out from the get-go.
Trump's reluctance to stand up to -- much less confront – Putin and Xi is not necessarily evidence of personal affinity alone, according to diplomatic observers; it reflects a transactional view of diplomacy in which personal relationships with powerful leaders are treated as instruments of statecraft, and immediate economic or political gains can outweigh the longer-term costs of accommodating strategic rivals.
Amid renewed jokes about Russian asset and Moscow's puppet, some experts have said the deal with Putin is “purely diplomatic” -- arguing that it was designed to put Ukrainian President Zelenskyy in a corner -- while others insist its main motivation is domestic In either case, the deal reinforces a familiar criticism of Trump: the appearance of a personal triumph over the painstaking construction of an effective strategy. Whether voters reward him will depend on what they see at the gas pump -- and if they believe the president has delivered results rather than another announcement. At present, the diesel deal looks less like a solution to Trump's midterm gambit than a small shipment carrying an outsized geopolitical cost.

In FocusWhy did Hong Kong’s 11 Skies fail and can the megaproject be rescued?
As New World Development returns control of the struggling project to the Airport Authority, experts examine the legal and economic ramifications
The roar of plane engines and the hustle and bustle at Hong Kong International Airport’s Terminal 2 present a stark contrast to the pin-drop silence at the adjacent 11 Skies commercial complex.
A South China Morning Post reporter who travelled between the two places in early October found minimal footfall at the shopping centre, with the bright and airy environment of the airport terminal replaced by dim, stuffy and boarded-up corridors, and poor air conditioning amid the simmering outdoor heat.
Occupying a gross floor area of 3.8 million square feet, 11 Skies is a mammoth project at the airport. Seventy per cent of the space was originally earmarked for a mall with 800 stores and 120 food and drink concepts, and the rest equally divided between experiential entertainment facilities and grade A office spaces.
But only one of its three office towers currently houses some companies running businesses at the airport.

India on Tuesday advised its nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain calm and vigilant amid an evolving security situation in the Gulf kingdom, urging them to follow local authorities’ instructions and avoid sharing videos or news related to the ongoing incidents. The advisory comes after a deadly attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 10 killed Indian national Mohammed Yousef Ali and injured several others, including Indian nationals. “In view of the current situation, all Indian nationals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia are advised to remain calm and vigilant, stay indoors in case of an aerial attack, and follow the instructions issued by local authorities through official channels,” the Indian Embassy said in its latest advisory. Quick answers to key questions The Embassy advised Indian nationals to remain calm and vigilant, follow instructions from local authorities through official channels, and stay indoors in case of an aerial attack. It also urged them not to circulate or repost videos and news about the incidents. The advisory asks Indian nationals to refrain from circulating or reposting videos and news related to the ongoing events. It does not give a specific reason for the request. Operations were suspended after attacks at the airport. Saudi authorities said the closure would allow them to complete procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of its facilities. Several Indian airlines suspended services until October 17. Air India and Air India Express cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah; IndiGo also suspended flights to and from Medina, while Akasa Air halted services to Riyadh and Jeddah. Passengers should check with their airline for the latest updates before travelling. IndiGo passengers were also advised to check their flight status before leaving for the airport. The mission also urged Indians to refrain from circulating or reposting videos and news related to the ongoing events. Mohammed Yousef Ali’s funeral was killed in Riyadh on October 12, according to the Indian Embassy. India’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia and other embassy officials attended the funeral and offered condolences to his family. “The funeral rites of late Mohammed Yousef Ali, who unfortunately lost his life in the Riyadh airport attack, were completed on October 12, 2026, in Riyadh, as per the wishes of his family,” the mission said. The embassy said it was continuing to monitor the condition of the injured Indian nationals and maintain contact with their families. As of the latest update, four injured Indians remained in intensive care, four were receiving treatment in regular hospital wards, and three had been discharged, as per PTI. . “Embassy officials continue to visit the hospitals where the injured Indian nationals are receiving medical treatment, and are in constant touch with their family members and providing all possible support,” the mission said. The Indian Embassy said Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation had announced the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Flight operations at other major airports, including Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, were continuing, although disruptions had been reported, the mission said. Several Indian airlines have suspended services to and from Saudi Arabia until October 17, according to information issued by the embassy on Tuesday. Air India and Air India Express suspended flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah. Akasa Air halted services to and from Riyadh and Jeddah, while IndiGo suspended flights connecting Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah and Medina. Passengers have been advised to check with their airlines for the latest updates before travelling. Saudi Arabia has faced a series of drone and missile attacks targeting civilian infrastructure, with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels identified as a threat amid escalating regional tensions. India’s supreme court has demanded accountability from the government and the senior election body over a controversial exercise that has led to the deletion of tens of millions of voters from the electoral roll and prompted mass protests.
Demonstrations have erupted across the country in recent days as opposition parties, student groups and the youth-led Cockroach movement have demanded the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, the head of the Election Commission of India (ECI).
They have accused Kumar of overseeing a direct attack on India’s democracy through an exercise to verify and “purify” the electoral roll in states across the country, which so far has led to 130 million names being removed. In Delhi, hundreds of people were detained as they tried to protest over the weekend.
On Monday, the supreme court issued notices to Narendra Modi’s government, the ECI and Kumar to demand answers over concerns raised about the voter list revision, saying they expected all “to respond in a clear, transparent manner”.
The ECI has claimed the exercise is simply cleaning electoral rolls of duplicate, dead and ineligible names, as well as removing “illegal infiltrators”. However, large numbers of people in Delhi and states such as Bihar and West Bengal say they have been wrongly stripped of their vote and have struggled to get it back.
There are accusations that revision of the electoral rolls particularly targets minorities such as Muslims, who are traditionally not voters of Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).
The opposition alliance, led by the Congress party, have accused the ECI of being hand in glove with the government over alleged vote “chori” or cheating. Kumar was chosen to head the ECI by a panel headed by Modi.
While the exercise, known as the special intensive revision (SIR), began last year, widespread outrage only recently erupted after a report in the Indian Express newspaper revealed multiple irregularities in the process, which were flagged in more than a dozen internal objections.
The two petitions taken up by the supreme court on Monday alleged that the credibility of the ECI was now in question and called for an independent inquiry into the decisions taken by Kumar in how the SIR process was conducted.
“Deletions of voters have been made in the largest democracy,” said Menaka Guruswamy, a lawyer acting for one of the petitioners. “We have grown up with free and fair elections, that is not the case now.”
Another advocate told the supreme court judges that if action was not taken to ensure that India’s electoral rolls remained fair, “this country will burn”. Another hearing in the cases will be held next week.
The controversies over the ECI have once again driven India’s young people on to the streets in protest, amid rising frustration at the Modi government.
The Cockroach Janata party (CJP), which led massive unrest over the summer that forced the resignation of Modi’s education minister, have once again mobilised and called for the resignation of Kumar. Thousands of CJP supporters took to the streets of Mumbai last Friday in protest and another demonstration was held on Saturday in Delhi.
In Delhi, police have been criticised for their heavy-handed approach to stopping any student groups protesting in the heart of the capital. Officers have been accused of sexually assaulting three journalists at the protests over the weekend and hundreds of young people were forced on to police buses. Delhi police said it was investigating the assault claims.

Astronomers have obtained the most detailed image to date of the Pa 30 nebula, the remnants of a supernova famous for having likely been observed and documented from Earth during the Middle Ages. Now, the new photograph reveals structures that had long gone unnoticed.
Previous images of the explosion’s remnants had also captured a sphere of long, filament-like strands of matter that collectively resemble fireworks or a dandelion. The new observations, made with the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii, revealed about 10 times more structures than any previous glimpses of the supernova remnant. With this resolution, researchers can now see that these filaments are not continuous as they had previously appeared. Instead, they’re shaped more like beads on a string, made up of pearl-like knots of gas of relatively uniform size.
These “cosmic pearls” are, in fact, enormous. According to the study published in The Astrophysical Journal, each bead measures about four light-days in diameter. “The planetary region of our solar system could fit in each knot about 10 times with room to spare,” Ilaria Caiazzo, a coauthor of the study, said in a press release. “The knots are quite strikingly uniform. We are excited to try to model them.”
How exactly the pearls formed is not yet entirely clear, though it’s assumed they are concentrations of material ejected during the explosion. What’s strange, however, is their regularity. In the aftermath of a supernova, astronomers expected to find much more oddly shaped accumulations, but the knots are similar in size and appear aligned along the filaments. This peculiar order is a new feature that could help researchers gain a deeper understanding of stellar death.
The Pa 30 nebula is also particularly unusual because the central star isn’t exactly dead. Instead, it’s considered a “zombie star.” Typically, a thermonuclear supernova is the violent death of a star, which is completely destroyed in the explosion. But in rare cases, part of the star may survive, and scientists do not yet fully understand how or why this happens. The unusual structures of Pa 30 could help astronomers reconstruct more precisely how these kinds of detonations occur and how zombie stars can live on afterward.
All of this has been discovered because scientists seem to have a bit of a crush on Pa 30. Few astronomical structures connect modern observation so directly with human accounts from more than eight centuries ago. The nebula matches the records left by Chinese and Japanese astronomers in 1181, who described the appearance of a new star in the sky that remained visible for several months. At the time, it was impossible to know that they were witnessing the aftermath of a massive stellar explosion. Centuries later, scientists linked that event to the supernova that gave rise to Pa 30.

The Trump administration warns Ukraine it could cut off intel, Zelenskyy tells NPR
KYIV, Ukraine — The Trump administration warned it could cut off intelligence-sharing with Ukraine unless Ukrainian forces stop long-range drone strikes on oil refineries inside Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NPR.
In an interview with NPR on Tuesday, Zelenskyy said the Trump administration's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel will not bring down fuel prices. He also refuted President Trump's assertion this weekend that Ukraine was to blame for the rise in diesel fuel prices. Zelenskyy pointed out it is because of the Iran war.
"Mostly people in the world know why their prices on any kind of energy, including diesel, raised up, why they increased. Because of Hormuz. Yes. Because of blocking the Strait of Hormuz," Zelenskyy said, referring to the vital shipping chokepoint between the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman.
President Zelenskyy's sit-down with NPR comes as Russia's full-scale invasion nears the five-year mark, at a time when the White House has renewed efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war. Tensions between Zelenskyy and President Trump have also flared up again after the U.S. made a key concession to Moscow.
On Friday, Trump moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Zelenskyy said in a statement it was a "a weak decision by strong partners."
Trump lashed back hard at Zelenskyy, saying, "I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," a leader who can reach a peace deal with Putin.
Then on Sunday, Trump announced on social media Russia and Ukraine had allegedly agreed to a partial ceasefire to halt attacks on each other's energy infrastructure — catching Kyiv by surprise — even as Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure continued.
Zelenskyy told NPR he found out about Trump's assertion of an energy ceasefire agreement "through social like you" — meaning, from Trump's post on his Truth Social account.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was asked Sunday about the announced energy truce and told reporters that contacts were ongoing.
Zelenskyy told NPR his country is striking Russian energy and logistics sites to weaken the Kremlin's ability to wage war. Ukraine wants the war to end, he said, but will not stop these strikes unless Russia stops attacking Ukrainian energy sites.
Putin doesn't respond to diplomacy, the Ukrainian leader said, "he understands force."
Meanwhile, high fuel prices have been a major concern in the U.S. as the midterm elections approach next month. In the U.S., diesel fuel costs an average of $6.27 per gallon — more than 70% above what it was a year ago when it was a little over $3.65 a gallon, according to AAA.
Zelenskyy said said Trump's decisions to temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel would not influence "the price in the United States. I'm sure … because the volume is not enough."
What it would do, he said, is provide the Kremlin with more money to spend on its war.
Last year, the Trump administration paused intelligence-sharing with Ukraine amid tensions with Zelenskyy. The White House did not comment on whether the administration has threatened to do so again, instead referring NPR to comments Trump made Tuesday. "We are helping them and we are sharing intel, we want the war to end. So, we're working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end," Trump told reporters.
Later, Zelenskyy described a new Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital. "A Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv. Once again, no early warning from our partners," he wrote on social media.
He said the target was a power plant, and added, "It is important that the United States really see what is happening and who is responsible for this war continuing."

Why Saudi Arabia has struggled to defend itself against the Houthis' recent attacks
Saudi Arabia has one of the world’s most expensive and sophisticated arsenals, filled with American warplanes, missile defenses and other technology

Saudi Arabia has one of the world’s most expensive and sophisticated arsenals, filled with American warplanes, missile defenses and other cutting-edge technology.
But in recent days it has appeared helpless in the face of barrages of missiles and drones fired by the Houthi rebel group from neighboring Yemen. The attacks have struck Saudi airports, killed at least 14 people and forced schoolchildren and businesspeople to stay indoors and work from home.
The Iran-backed Houthis, once seen as little more than a ragtag militia, have grown into a formidable fighting force. They have inflicted damage on the region’s top oil producer, threatened critical supply routes in the Red Sea and now risk reigniting a full-scale war on the Arabian Peninsula that displaced millions and killed tens of thousands.
The Houthis are attacking Saudi Arabia because it supports government forces in Yemen the rebels seek to overthrow. As Saudi Arabia investigates how its air defenses failed to stop the Houthis' attacks, it must also consider how to respond and what the rebels might do next.
Here’s what we know and don’t know about the Saudi and Houthi conflict:
Saudi Arabia has a vast arsenal of US weapons
Saudi Arabia is the world’s top purchaser of American weapons, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. It says the Saudis received 12% of all U.S. arms exports from 2021-2025.
Over the years, the Saudis have purchased American F-15 warplanes, Patriot air defense systems, as well as advanced radars and offensive missile systems, according to the think tank, which tracks global arms transfers.
Saudi Arabia's annual budget for 2026 listed $83 billion for military expenditures. Earlier this year, it struck a $9 billion deal with Washington for 730 Patriot missiles.
But it has a huge area to defend
The Houthis have been able to exploit Saudi Arabia's large size.
Vulnerable energy, civilian and military assets are scattered across the country's sparsely populated territory roughly three times the size of Texas. Its border with Yemen stretches more than 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) through rugged desert areas.
“Expecting a country the size of Saudi Arabia to intercept every missile is simply unrealistic. No defense can guarantee complete protection,” Ali Shihabi, a Saudi analyst, said in a post online Monday.
At the same time, regional officials say that Saudi Arabia is running low on interceptors and has reached out to allies for help.
Saudi Arabia recently struck a joint defense pact with Pakistan and Turkey. But so far, the two countries appear to be largely staying on the sidelines or limiting their support.
President Donald Trump said this week he is evaluating whether the U.S. should join Saudi strikes on the Houthis. But he has not yet announced a decision.
Houthi weapons and tactics are battle-tested
Like their patron Iran, the Houthis have deployed asymmetric warfare for the 21st century by capitalizing on their strengths — primarily drones and missiles. For the Houthis, success on the battlefield doesn’t require toppling Saudi Arabia; disrupting the Saudi economy and sowing fear within its society may be enough to give the Houthis leverage in any possible negotiations to end the fighting.
The Houthis have a large arsenal capable of striking targets well over 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometers) away. Some warheads change direction during flight and pose an extra challenge to air defenses.
The group has fired hundreds of drones and missiles at Israel since its war in Gaza erupted in October 2023. While most were intercepted, a handful managed to land, in one case killing an Israeli man. Another strike hit an Israeli airport last year.
Andreas Krieg, a professor at King’s College London, said this experience in challenging Israel’s cutting-edge air defenses has given the Houthis confidence and expertise as they now strike Saudi Arabia.
“They’ve learned how to over-saturate the radars,” he said.
The Houthis, working with allied militias in Iraq, have also targeted Saudi oil installations, including a vital pipeline used to export oil through the Red Sea while movement through the Strait of Hormuz is limited. The Houthis have also seized territory in Yemen near the Bab el-Mandeb, a key Red Sea waterway, putting additional pressure on Saudi oil exports.
Saudi Arabia appears to have miscalculated
Michael Ratney, a former U.S. ambassador to Saudi Arabia, says the kingdom assumed the Houthis wouldn’t strike civilian targets like airports. Doing so marked “a paradigm shift,” he said.
Ratney, now an adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said the Saudis now find themselves in a position where they have to respond while also trying to prevent the fighting from spinning out of control.
“They can’t not strike back — they were attacked in a very brutal way by their archenemies,” he said. “They need to exert military pressure on the Houthis and then find a way to kind of deescalate.”
Rather than sending troops into Yemen, the Saudis will likely launch airstrikes against the Houthis and ramp up support of nationalist forces, several analysts said.
“It will be surrogate warfare,” Krieg said.
The Houthis are now a formidable force
While the Houthis don't have the firepower of Saudi Arabia, they have grown into a fearsome force controlling roughly one-third of Yemen thanks to help from Iran.
The United Nations estimates that the Houthis by 2024 had recruited up to 350,000 fighters. That's up from just 30,000 in 2015, when Saudi Arabia intervened in the internationally recognized Yemeni government's civil war against the Houthis and imposed a naval blockade.
Ratney says the Houthis now have a “symbiotic relationship” with Iran and should not be seen as an Iranian puppet.
The strikes on Saudi airports and economic assets symbolize a sharing of lessons in asymmetric warfare between the Houthis and the Iranians: how to not just puncture expensive air defenses, but also damage vulnerable energy installations and threaten global maritime routes.
“Over the course of the past few years, the Iranians have been innovating and sharing that with the Houthis and it’s gone both ways. The Houthis have been innovating, and sharing it with the Iranians,” Ratney said. “It’s no coincidence that they’ve ended up with a similar approach.”
Their recent military successes have made the Houthis feel “untouchable,” said Farea Al-Muslimi, a fellow at Chatham House focused on Yemen.
“It’s very hard to convince a man he’s going on the wrong side if he just moved forward and he has a gun in his hand,” he said. But the Houthis are now likely to suffer a brutal Saudi counterattack, he said.

Google’s screenless Fitbit Air made a splash, but it’s been three years since the company updated its display-equipped Charge 6. That older tracker is showing its age, lacking newer automatic workout detection, deeper health metrics, and an IP68 rating. That's where the new Fitbit Edge comes in.
Announced on Monday, it is the successor fitness tracker fans with a screen preference have been waiting for. It sits in a sweet spot at $180—not as costly as a Google Pixel Watch but offering a similar experience in a slimmer, pill-shaped design. And unlike the Pixel Watch, it's compatible with Android and iPhones via the Google Health app. Preorders are available now, and it goes on sale on October 27.
The Fixable Fitbit
The Edge has a user-replaceable battery, a Fitbit first, aligning with Google’s efforts to make its Pixel Watch more repairable. (Likely also due to new battery regulations set to take effect next year in the European Union.) Repair options will vary by region and availability.
If you find the Pixel Watch’s round face too bulky, the Edge's capsule-shaped alternative might suit smaller wrists better. If the Charge 6’s 1.04-inch display was too small, the Edge upgrades it to a larger 1.34-inch screen. The difference is noticeable, and that extra real estate could make a real impact when glancing at your metrics mid-workout.
The Edge borrows a few more attributes from the Pixel Watch, including an altimeter that uses atmospheric pressure to measure elevation changes. That means it can record elevation gain and loss during outdoor activities, track floors climbed, and add more context to your outdoor stats. It also has a far-field skin temperature sensor, replacing the standard device temperature sensor found in other Fitbits. By bringing some of the Pixel Watch’s more advanced hardware to a fitness-first wearable, Google is giving the Edge a compelling middle-ground position in its lineup at a Fitbit-friendly price.
The Edge inherits the Fitbit Air’s improvements while restoring several Charge 6 features the screenless tracker lacks, including built-in GPS and electrical sensors that work with the electrocardiogram (ECG) app. You can also control music playback on a connected Bluetooth device, as you could with the Charge 6, and Google Maps turn-by-turn directions will arrive later this year.
Google also announced more advanced automatic activity tracking for the Edge, using Gemini Intelligence to identify up to 100 workout types. It can track more than 50 exercise modes, up from 40 on its predecessor. Google will also roll out these features to the Pixel Watch 5 and Air. If they work as promised, it means users won't have to log every activity manually.
With a Google Health Premium subscription, the Edge can track blood pressure trends without manual calibration and insulin resistance trends without requiring a blood draw. Google first announced these capabilities alongside the Pixel Watch 5's debut, but they only became available at the end of September. They’re also available on the Air, keeping Google’s screenless tracker up to date as its lineup expands.
The seven-day battery life remains unchanged, but it’s one of the Edge’s biggest advantages over the Pixel Watch. Like the Air, it takes about 90 minutes to fully charge, which is half an hour less than the Charge 6.
One odd omission is a near-field communication (NFC) sensor, which means the Edge doesn’t support contactless payments through Google Wallet. That’s a downgrade from the Charge 6 and a strange function to lose on a fitness tracker that Google is pitching as a step up from its basic Fitbits.
Dressed for Every Occasion
The Edge introduces new digital and analog clock faces, and the Canyon band color returns from the Pixel Watch 5, alongside five other band styles (Active Band, Active Sport Band, Performance Loop Band, Magnet Band, and Metal Links Band). The Stephen Curry collaboration ($220), which also appeared with the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5, is back in the same brown-orange color.
Alongside the Edge, Google is also giving the screenless Fitbit Air a visual upgrade with a new Metal Mesh band. It’s an even dressier strap than the polyurethane Elevated Modern Band. The Air may have initially been designed to disappear on your wrist, but the new band makes it a statement accessory.
If you’re all in on the screenless Fitbit Air, the Edge won’t change your mind. But if you’re not ready to give up a display, the Edge might be a compelling and affordable alternative for both iPhone and Android users. Stay tuned for our review.
