EXCLUSIVE: The New York Times’ prestigious Op-Docs platform has acquired The Revolution Against Death, the new short film directed by two-time Oscar nominee Joshua Oppenheimer.
The documentary set at an annual longevity conference known as the Revolution Against Aging and Death Festival will be co-released globally in early December by New York Op-Docs and MUBI. It premiered at the Tampere Film Festival in Finland and recently screened at the Telluride Film Festival.
At sessions as part of the Revolution Against Aging and Death Festival, “fear is in the air — of illness, of invisibility, of dying alone,” notes a release. “Directed by Oppenheimer, the film offers a visceral portrait of aging, death and the quest for immortality.”
Oppenheimer (The Look of Silence, The Act of Killing) is no mere impartial observer of the festival proceedings.
Watch on Deadline
“Haunted by a fear of death since I was a child, I traveled to a gathering of would-be immortals,” he writes of the film project. “I recognized myself, clinging white-knuckled to the hope that I might defeat death. In the years that followed, I discovered that because nothing lasts, everything matters — and eternity lies in change itself. This film is my poem about that journey.”
In a statement, Op-Docs Executive Producer Alexandra Garcia commented, “We are honored to bring Joshua Oppenheimer’s work to the Op-Docs audience with this unique film that is a haunting, observational look at the fundamental human conflict between the reality of death and the relentless drive for immortality.”
The Revolution Against Death joins seven other films on Op-Docs’s 2026 slate of awards contenders, including Living With a Visionary, winner of the Short Film Jury Award for Animation at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival; The Tuners, winner of a Silver Dragon at the 2026 Krakow Film Festival, and A Wolf in the Suburbs, which premiered at SXSW this year. Op-Docs won an Academy Award for its 2021 short The Queen of Basketball, directed by Ben Proudfoot. The series has claimed seven Oscar nominations, including in 2025 for Instruments of a Beating Heart, directed by Ema Ryan Yamazaki, and in 2024 for Island In Between, directed by S. Leo Chaing.
The Revolution Against Death screens Saturday at the Chicago International Film Festival and next month at IDFA in Amsterdam, the world’s biggest documentary film festival.
Oppenheimer is the recipient of a MacArthur Fellowship, widely known as the “genius grant,” that is awarded to “extraordinarily talented and creative individuals as an investment in their potential.” The filmmaker made his fiction debut in 2024 with The End, a post-apocalyptic musical thriller starring Tilda Swinton, Michael Shannon, and George MacKay.
The New York Times Op-Docs is a collection of more than 450 short films that “have sparked global conversations, influenced national policies and garnered an array of industry distinctions, including Emmy Awards, Peabody Awards and an Oscar.” Alexandra Garcia is executive producer of the series and Yvonne Ashley Kouadjo is the producer.

Everstone Capital-backed EV startup GreenCell Mobility has raised ₹330 Cr ($34.6 Mn) in an equity funding round led by Impact Fund Denmark to support the rollout of about 4,500 electric buses currently under deployment. The Mumbai-based startup is eyeing expanding its fleet to more than 5,000 e-buses across 105 cities across India. “Our focus is on executing our order book with rigour, strengthening service delivery and ensuring that the organisation keeps pace with the size and complexity of our operations. This equity investment gives us greater headroom to accelerate our plans while maintaining the standards of reliability, efficiency and customer experience that are fundamental to our business,” GreenCell Mobility managing director and chief executive Devndra Chawla said. Founded in 2019, GreenCell Mobility focuses on deploying and operating electric buses for public transportation. It acquires electric buses via contract manufacturing arrangements with vendors and then deploys them for both intercity and intracity travel. Backed by Eversource Capital, a joint venture between Everstone Capital and Lightsource, GreenCell primarily operates under the brand NueGo. It claims to operate more than 1,200 electric buses in India, including 900 on intra-city routes, 300 under its NueGo brand for inter-city travel, and 50 for MSRTC. The startup also runs over 270 charging stations to support its fleet. The startup previously raised $37 Mn from World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and also counts Eversource Capital, British International Investment and Tata Capital among its backers. India’s electric bus segment has so far drawn strong interest from development finance institutions and lenders backing vehicle deployments under long-term public transport contracts. GreenCell’s latest round suggested that investors are also beginning to back the operating platform layer in the category, not just asset financing. The investment highlights the role of institutional capital in expanding electric public transportation infrastructure in India. Large-scale electric bus deployments require funding not only for vehicles but also for the operational capabilities and charging infrastructure needed to support them. Earlier in March, electric bus manufacturer PMI Electro Mobility, along with its electric bus platform Allfleet, has signed a definitive agreement with private equity giant KKR for an investment commitment of up to $310 Mn, to help scale the electric bus platform and focus on expanding its presence across India. PMI subsequently filed for an IPO via the confidential route last month.

Cornell University bans frat parties, vows to address 'disturbing' campus culture
Cornell University has banned parties and social events at fraternities for the rest of the school year and will bring sexual assault investigators into its police unit, in response to a former student's allegation of gang rape in 2024.
The changes came on Tuesday as the university said it is committed to addressing a "deeply disturbing" culture of drug and alcohol abuse, and a rise in sexual violence on campus following a civil lawsuit filed by a former student, Jane Doe, which set off national outrage and a crisis at Cornell.
"I am deeply sorry for the harm Jane Doe suffered in 2024, and appalled that this act of sexual violence occurred within our Cornell community," Michael I. Kotlikoff, who is Cornell's president, wrote in a letter addressed to the campus on Tuesday. "It is clear that women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe. We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action."
The lawsuit, which Doe filed nearly one month ago, alleges that Doe was plied with ketamine and was sexually assaulted by members of the Chi Phi fraternity during a party in October of 2024. The details of the allegations, which disclosed how fraternity members used a Snapchat group chat to discuss the woman and events at the party with openly crude language, sparked fury across the nation.
Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, told news outlets that Doe has been sent death threats and police swarmed her family's home since she filed the lawsuit.
The administration's changes come after student groups organized protests last week on campus.
"The administration is clearly feeling the heat and needed to make a move," says John Hartnett, a sophomore at Cornell who has helped organize protests. He called the changes a "half measure," and said that banning frats was not a long term solution to systematic issues at the university.
The faculty senate is considering a vote of no confidence in the university administration at a meeting scheduled for Wednesday. It's a rare move that demonstrates the deep seated frustration and distrust stemming from the 2024 case.
"Trust is still eroded on campus — that hasn't changed," says Julia Chang, an associate professor of Hispanic studies in the Department of Romance Studies. "The fact that these changes are coming about now — two years later — is a testament to the power of the student movement and the global conversation it has sparked; not the integrity of the administration."
The moratorium on events at fraternities is expected to have a reverberating effect on campus, where about one-third of all students participate in fraternities and sororities. The university's ties to Greek life, Kotlikoff said, has in part created a toxic culture on campus that requires serious course correction.
"While this is not a problem unique to Cornell, we are committed to setting a higher standard for education, oversight, and enforcement of safe social behavior and citizenship," Kotlikoff wrote.
Ray Epstein, who works with a consent education company, and is one of the organizers of a rally planned just steps away from Cornell's campus on Tuesday, said that while the measures from Cornell are "overall a win," they also serve as an "effort to save face."
"What I think they should be doing, is operating first instead of as a business, the way that they are now, as institutions that are meant to educate and keep their students safe," Epstein said.
Kotlikoff said that in addition to enhancing bystander training programming, the university will also improve its services to survivors of sexual assault by increasing staffing in its civil rights office, which would help individuals navigate the reporting process for incidents.
Additionally, the university will work with the New York State Police's criminal investigators on campus sexual assault investigations. The move allows the investigators, who are independent from the university, to take on cases in which survivors pursue criminal charges.
The university plans to bring in faculty who are experts in sexual assault and rape culture to help reform the Presidential Task Force on Sexual Assault through listening events with the Cornell community.
Kotlikoff's letter did not explain why these events are only being issued now — two years after administrators at Cornell learned about the allegations in 2024.
Although the district attorney did not prosecute the case in 2024, Cornell's Title IX office conducted an investigation in 2025. In March 2025, a panel of staff and faculty at Cornell moved to expel or suspend some of the men. The panel required the remaining men to write "essays" in addition to other sanctions.
Cornell also barred the Chi Phi fraternity chapter, which was closed in 2024.

Isle of Wight fossil sheds light on enigmatic meat-eating dinosaurs
Oct 13 : The partial skull of a tiger-sized predator that prowled what is now the Isle of Wight off England's southern coast about 120 million years ago is giving scientists a better understanding of an enigmatic group of meat-eating dinosaurs known for running down prey and ripping them apart with massive hand claws.
Researchers said the fossil belongs to a species they have named Invictibellatrix amberina, an early member of the lineage of Cretaceous Period carnivorous dinosaurs called megaraptorans. Invictibellatrix adds to the knowledge of skull anatomy among early megaraptorans and, being the first one known from Europe, helps show how the group spread globally.
Invictibellatrix is one of the smallest megaraptorans. Based on fossils of closely related megaraptorans, the researchers estimated that Invictibellatrix was about 16 feet (5 meters) long, with the weight of a large tiger. Its body may have been covered in filament-like feathers, they said.
Megaraptorans were part of the group called theropods that spans all the meat-eating dinosaurs.
"Megaraptorans are very unique among theropods because they have relatively small and slender heads but had long and strong arms with massive hand claws as well as very lightly built skeletons," said Cassius Morrison, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Leeds in England and lead author of the study published in the journal Royal Society Open Science.
"These characteristics imply that megaraptorans were agile hunters capable of chasing down prey and using their large arms and claws to catch them and disembowel them using their hand claws," Morrison said.
The largest-known megaraptoran, named Maip, was about 33 feet (10 meters) long, inhabiting Patagonia during the twilight of the dinosaur age, about 50 million years after Invictibellatrix lived.
Littler megaraptorans like Invictibellatrix may have hunted smaller prey like mammals, smaller reptiles and baby dinosaurs. Larger megaraptorans may have targeted bigger plant-eating dinosaurs like duckbilled hadrosaurs and long-necked sauropods, though probably not the biggest ones.
Megaraptorans hunted in the opposite way from massive predators like Tyrannosaurus rex. Tyrannosaurus employed its large and stoutly built head, enormous teeth and incredible bite strength to kill prey, but had puny arms of little use in hunting.
Invictibellatrix was not the Isle of Wight's top predator, with larger theropods around, alongside various herbivorous dinosaurs, and may have filled a role similar to a hyena today.
There is a debate among dinosaur paleontologists as to where megaraptorans fit on the theropod family tree. Despite differences in how they were built and hunted, one hypothesis is that megaraptorans were closely related to tyrannosaurs, the group that included Tyrannosaurus and others that dominated the landscapes in North America and Asia later in the Cretaceous.
'UNCONQUERED FEMALE WARRIOR'
Invictibellatrix means "unconquered female warrior." Morrison noted that after humble beginnings megaraptorans developed into apex predators in South America, Australia and Antarctica, becoming "the ruling queens," while the tyrannosaurs became the "tyrant kings" in North America and Asia.
Scientists are trying to unravel the evolutionary history of megaraptorans. A leading hypothesis has megaraptorans originating in Asia before migrating through Europe into Africa and then on into South America, thriving until the dinosaurs were doomed by an asteroid strike 66 million years ago. This hypothesis was lacking fossil evidence because no megaraptorans had been known from Europe until now.
"These findings help to uncover the evolution of one of the most mysterious theropod groups," University College London doctoral student and study co-author Charlie Scherer said.
The Invictibellatrix fossil, a fragmented braincase, was discovered about a century ago and acquired by the Natural History Museum in London in 1924.
"It was left in one of the collection's drawers ever since, and no one noticed it until a couple of years ago," Scherer said.
While Tyrannosaurus may be more imposing than Invictibellatrix, the researchers noted that if a person were somehow transported back in time — like in the recent film "The End of Oak Street" — Invictibellatrix might present more of a danger.
"A smaller theropod like Invictibellatrix would likely have been a much bigger threat to a human than something like T. rex because we would likely be too small for T. rex to see as a worthwhile meal because of how massive it was and the amount of energy it would be required to catch us," Morrison said.
"But we would be the perfect size for something smaller like Invictibellatrix, as we are about a third to a quarter of its weight, making us a good hearty meal and more than just a snack. Additionally, Invictibellatrix would have the agility and maneuverability to pursue and catch a human."

Qantas flight grounded after bedbug outbreak
- Published
A Qantas flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled on Saturday, after an outbreak of bedbugs on the plane.
During the previous flight on Friday - a nearly 17-hour journey from Perth to Rome - some passengers had complained that they were being bitten by bugs, according to the Sydney Morning Herald.
They were reportedly given antihistamines to help ease the itch of the bites, but supplies ran out.
The Boeing 787 Dreamliner had to be grounded for "a deep clean", a Qantas spokesperson told the BBC.
"We sincerely apologise to customers for the cancellation of Saturday's Rome to Perth service, which allowed our engineers and maintenance teams to carry out a deep clean of the aircraft after an issue was identified on a small number of economy seats," the spokesperson said.
All affected customers were provided with accommodation and were rebooked on alternative flights within 48 hours of their original departure, the carrier said.
Bedbugs are small, wingless parasites that can live on clothes, furniture and bedding. Their bites can be itchy but they do not usually cause more serious health problems, the NHS website says, external.
But they can be difficult and expensive to get rid of. Treatment includes washing all bedding, clothing, and household materials like curtains on a hot wash and tumble dry, or they can be put in plastic bags in a freezer for three or four days.
Bedbugs causing travel chaos is not unusual - less than two weeks ago, several Southeastern train services in England were cancelled after drivers discovered the creepy-crawlies in their cabs.
In 2017, British Airways apologised to a family travelling from Vancouver to London, after they were left covered in bug bites from an overnight flight.
And Turkish Airlines faced with a PR nightmare last year after the New York Times reported, external of several instances of bedbug infestations on its planes - and allegations at the time that the airline did nothing about it.

Two Indian cartoonists, Satish Acharya and Manjul, recently revealed that their Instagram accounts and posts were withheld in India, following orders from the government. While the former’s account was restored on October 6, the latter’s post remains unavailable in India.
On September 23, The Indian Express reported that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 formal objections over 10 months to decisions concerning electoral-roll management and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), including changes to Form 6, voter deletions and restorations, the centralisation of electoral-roll data, and appeals against decisions in West Bengal.
The investigation, based on internal notes and correspondence reviewed by the newspaper, showed that the two commissioners repeatedly said certain decisions had been taken without their knowledge or approval by chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, with Sandhu at one point describing an SIR-related change as “unauthorised and illegal.” Both Acharya and Manjul had posted cartoons satirising this case.
ALSO READ: Instagram takes down content critical of Vizag data centre projects, cites IT Act notices
On September 23, Acharya posted an illustration on Kumar and the SIR controversy. Five days later, on September 28, his account was restricted in India.
However, his profile was still available on Facebook and X, and the said toon was still visible on both platforms.
After his account was banned, on September 28, Acharya posted screenshots of notifications received by Meta, which said that several of his earlier satirical posts were also being banned in India under Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000.
On the same day, he posted the screenshot of his account getting restricted in India, contrasting it with a screenshot of Modi’s comment that “cartoons have healing power and cartoonists are closer to God”.
Speaking to Alt News, Acharya said he found out about his account being restricted while checking news reports on the increasing banning of accounts critical of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government. “I thought of checking my own Instagram account status and found that a list of posts were restricted in India, some of them were posted in 2023-24. By the end of day, I found that my entire profile has been restricted in India,” he said.
“For the last one decade, I have regularly faced restrictions on my cartoons on different social media platforms. (Their) aim was to restrict the reach…mostly during elections or major protests like CAA protests & farmers’ protests. This is the first time that my entire profile was restricted in India. It’s quite shameful that they (the government) are scared that the narratives created by the regime over the last two decades will be demolished by cartoons, journalists, and comedians,” he added.
He said that his reach has been affected after the ban, adding that he written to Meta’s grievance cell.

He also posted the notice from Instagram, which claimed that this particular post’s access has been restricted in India “pursuant to a notice from the Government of India/Law enforcement”. (Archive)

A report by The Indian Express, published on August 18, revealed that between March and July, the government issued a blocking order for online content every 68 seconds on average, which amounted to 1,275 such cases daily and around 2 lakh cases over a period of five months.
According to that report, this government takedowns surged specifically after the Cockroach Janta Party-led students’ protest against the NEET exam irregularities in June and July. Although the government took down social media posts from Facebook, Instagram and YouTube as well, Instagram faced maximum content restrictions given that its user demographic is mostly the Gen-Z. According to the report, out of the total blocking orders, 1,00,000 such orders were for Instagram only while Facebook and YouTube accounted for 80,000 and 15,000 takedown orders, respectively.
ALSO READ: Government orders trigger sweeping Instagram censorship days after CJP protest
Alt News had earlier reported that in February, the government amended the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. The amendment reduced the time available to social media platforms to remove or disable access to unlawful content from 36 hours to three hours after receiving a valid court order or a “reasoned intimation” from the appropriate government or its authorised agency. This change was notified through a press brief on July 22.
Although the order focused predominantly on countering harms caused by AI generated content and information, critics believe that the amendments have served as a tool to curb anti-establishment content. In our reportage, we found that most of the blocking orders were issued through the Union Home Ministry’s Sahyog portal, a platform created to send such notices, under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, 2000. These orders were issued by various central and state government agencies. Meta has also integrated its Application Programming Interface (API) with the Sahyog portal, enabling content flagged through government directions to be automatically removed from its platforms without being reviewed by a human executive.

The Sentinelese, living on North Sentinel Island in the Bay of Bengal, are one of the most isolated peoples on earth.
Part of an archipelago governed by India, it is prohibited by law to venture within 5km of their island. And when a missionary did manage to land on the beach in 2018, he was killed by bow and arrow.
Yet none of that was to deter influencer Mykhailo Polyakov, who last year filmed himself arriving on North Sentinel Island, and leaving a can of coke on the beach.
Features writer Elle Hunt documents the rise of a new breed of influencer, travelling around the world, and streaming to millions their attempts to contact the uncontacted – despite the warnings of indigenous rights groups that the consequences could be fatal, both for the social media stars and the communities they risk exposing to disease.
Helen Pidd also speaks to Ecuadorian indigenous rights activist María José Andrade Cerda about the rights and wrongs of this new world.

A woman who claimed to be a niece of former chief minister Mamata Banerjee allegedly tried to enter her security cordon with a knife in an intoxicated state on Tuesday evening, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress claimed.
Party MP Dola Sen sent a written complaint to the Kalighat police station in Kolkata stating that the incident took place around 6 pm near Banerjee’s residence in Kalighat.
“This is to inform you that around 6 pm on Tuesday, a lady named Tannishtha Saha, reportedly known as a civic volunteer and a drug addict, came with a violent mode and attacked Mamata Banerjee with a knife and furthermore claimed herself as her niece,” Sen stated in her letter to the officer-in-charge of Kalighat police station.
Banerjee had come out of her house to inaugurate a Durga Puja pandal near her residence when the woman tried to enter the security cordon from behind.
“When I asked her identity, she said that Banerjee was her paternal aunt. I refused to let her in. She then tried to sneak into the security cordon from the front. When she failed, she lay down on the road and started hurling abuses. It was then that we saw that she had a knife,” Sen said.
A TMC leader said that the woman was overpowered by TMC workers around Banerjee and later handed over to the police.
No senior police officials, including Rahul De, deputy commissioner of police (south), responded to calls and messages.

In October, rumors circulated that U.S. President Donald Trump's administration did not extend an invitation to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, an international body that aims to preserve democracy and human rights across the globe, to observe the 2026 midterm elections.
The OSCE explains that its goal in observing elections is to "assess the extent to which fundamental freedoms are respected in the campaign and if the elections are characterized by equality, universality, political pluralism, confidence, transparency and accountability."
Social media users who shared the claim noted that it was the first time since 2002, when the OSCE first started observing U.S. elections, that the group had not received an invitation. One post featured an image of Trump with text reading, "Trump demands 'secure' elections, yet rejects independent scrutiny and offers no explanation. Perhaps security was never the point."
The rumor circulated after Trump's Department of Justice said it would deploy its own election monitors, sparking concerns from Trump's opponents.
The claim was true.
In a statement posted to its website Sept. 23. the OSCE confirmed that the U.S. had not invited it to observe the 2026 midterm elections.
"The decision not to invite the OSCE to observe the 2026 midterm congressional elections in the United States is regrettable, particularly given the long-standing co-operation with the country in the field of election observation," the organization said.
They wrote that the decision was "not in line with the 1990 Copenhagen Document," which the group describes as an outline of basic human rights and freedoms that "broadens the scope of human rights matters to include election commitments" and "recognizes that the presence of international observers can enhance the electoral process."
The OSCE confirmed in its statement that the 2026 midterms marked the first time it was not invited to observe a federal U.S. election since the group first began observing elections in the country in 2002. That year, the OSCE sent representatives to the Florida gubernatorial election. 
The 2002 observation occurred after the contentious 2000 presidential election between George W. Bush and Al Gore that resulted in a recount in Florida. The matter ultimately ended up with the Supreme Court, and the United States didn't see a president-elect officially declared until that December.
According to a 2004 article by the Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe about the history of the U.S. inviting OSCE to observe elections, following its 2002 observation in Florida, OSCE observed the 2003 California gubernatorial recall election that actor Arnold Schwarzenegger won. 
OSCE said it has observed 12 federal elections, including six midterms, since 2002.
The CSCE wrote in 2004 that the U.S. had formally invited observers to its elections in 1996, 1998, 2000 and 2002, noting that 2002 was the first election that OSCE had observed. 
In the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections in November, Trump continued his attempts to implement voting restrictions and pitched giving Americans $5,000 each if Republicans won, sparking opposition from critics.
A White House official told Snopes via email that "no other nation has done more to advance the cause of human freedom and representative government" than the United States and added, "American elections will be administered, participated in, and observed by American citizens."
The White House did not deny that it had declined an invite to OSCE observers and provided no explanation for departing from decades of precedent.
We reached out to the OSCE and the Justice Department for further comment and will update this article if we receive responses.
For further reading, we fact-checked a claim that Trump thanked billionaire Elon Musk for artificially increasing votes for Republicans ahead of the 2026 midterms.

20 December 2024 was a crucial moment for Luxembourg in supporting WHO and strengthening global public health, to make progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals in 2025–2028. A Strategic Partnership Framework (SPF) with the Ministry of Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Affairs was signed amounting to €46.5 million – the largest-ever agreement WHO has had with Luxembourg. Furthermore, the first-ever multiyear agreement with the Ministry of Health and Social Safety €1 million was launched, as the country’s first voluntary contribution to WHO.
Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General greets with Luxembourg's Martine Deprez, Minister of Health and Social Safety and Xavier Bettel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Cooperation and Foreign Trade. © MAE Luxembourg
“From now till 2028, this contribution will help finance priority areas in Luxembourg’s collaboration with WHO” said Martine Deprez, Minister of Health and Social Safety during the bilateral meeting, “notably for sanitary crisis preparedness and response and the fight against health inequalities, with a special focus on gender.”
The amount of €46.5 million contains fully flexible and thematic funding, and allocations for the Universal Health Coverage Partnership, tropical disease research and polio eradication. The fully flexible funding enables WHO to allocate the money to the areas of highest need.
“By signing two new partnership agreements, we have reaffirmed Luxembourg's continued support for the WHO and its mission,” said Xavier Bettel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Cooperation and Foreign Trade. “This reflects our strong commitment to promoting global health and multilateralism. We launch these agreements with WHO because we believe the best way to avoid is to prevent.”
To support the achievement of WHO’s priorities, the strategic partnership framework with Luxembourg includes support for WHO’s core work to develop, deliver and implement high-quality technical products – the guidelines, norms and standards on which many countries rely.
Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, remarked how symbolic it was that the agreements were signed on the International Day of Solidarity. They are “a strong statement of solidarity by Luxembourg, not just with WHO, but with the people of the world”, said Dr Tedros.
Xavier Bettel, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and Martine Deprez at the signing ceremony. © MAE Luxembourg
WHO and Luxembourg continue their historical strategic partnership, collaborating to fulfill a shared mission to promote, provide and protect health.

Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
As a result of the strong El Niño, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.
Isaias is expected to make landfall on Friday evening local time, bringing an estimated 75-150mm (2.9-5.9in) of rainfall across the Gulf coast. There may be up to 250mm in places, with a possibility of flash flooding and isolated river flooding.
The NOAA also said there was increasing likelihood of life-threatening storm surge along portions of the northern Gulf coast and damaging hurricane-force winds over portions of the Florida panhandle, southern Alabama and Mississippi. A hurricane warning has been issued and people have been told to prepare for long power outages and to obey any evacuation orders issued.
In Zimbabwe, a state of disaster was declared in the south-east Masvingo province on Tuesday after a severe hailstorm caused widespread damage to homes and critical infrastructure.
Preliminary assessments found the roofs had been torn off 8,500 homes. A further 15,300 people reported shattered windows, leaving many exposed to the elements as the rainy season begins.
The country’s power infrastructure was badly affected, disrupting drainage and sewerage systems, raising concerns about public health.

I’ve Been Tracking My Weight for Years. These Are the Best Smart Scales
Featured in this article
After years of sleepiness, the smart scale world has finally woken up—driven almost certainly by the GLP-1 craze, as millions of consumers find themselves wondering if those weekly jabs are actually working.
What was previously a category occupied by dated gear has abruptly exploded, and for good reason. Today’s smart scales don’t just report on your weight; they do things like measure your heart rate and break down muscle composition, and some can even give you an eye on your heart health, courtesy of technology like integrated ECG systems. Through mobile apps, they can track all of this information over time.
The big shift in the category in the past year has been a flood of new full-body scanners hitting the market from all corners. Essentially bathroom scales with handlebar-based scanners, these don’t just use bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) to measure conductivity (and, thus, body fat percentage) through your feet. They can now scan through your hands, too, giving you a much more holistic (and ostensibly accurate) look at your body metrics than a floor scale will provide. I’ve personally seen body fat percentage numbers swing up to 6 percent between the two types of scales. (Spoiler: The full-body scanner data is always higher.)
Do you really need all that information? I’ve long suggested that it’s really the trend line that matters most, not the absolute numbers, and as long as your metrics are headed in the right direction, it doesn’t matter quite as much whether things are off by a small percentage. Consistent weigh-ins are the most important part of the process, along with tracking that information over time to determine whether your diet and workout regimen (or medication routine) is getting you the results you need.
Mind you, scale prices are headed up, and new full-body scanners can now top $600 for top-tier tech. That’s part of the reason why I still recommend a standard scale for most users, as these devices are considerably less expensive, and the results they offer are likely to be good enough for all but serious athletes.
Either way, this roundup has an option for every type of user.
Updated October 2026: I've added Withings’ BodyScan 2 and new honorable mentions from Runstar, Tanita, and Withings. I've also added scales to avoid and ensured up-to-date prices throughout.
How Do Smart Scales Work?
Smart scales come in two basic flavors: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. The former connects directly to your phone to sync its readings. The latter uses your home’s wireless network to sync readings straight to the cloud, which your phone’s app can then access. Wi-Fi scales are generally more expensive but more versatile. While older scales often featured erratic wireless connections, newer models have many of their kinks worked out—and firmware updates have improved connectivity.
Virtually all smart scales use the same type of system to gauge your additional vitals: bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), which involves sending a minuscule electric current up one leg and measuring what happens when it comes down the other side. Some mathematical magic converts all of this into any number of derived measurements about things like your body’s percentage of fat, water, and bone; body-mass index (BMI); and, sometimes, arcana like your basal metabolic rate (BMR), which is a measure of your body’s energy consumption at rest. All the scales I tested can sync data with Apple Health and Google's Health Connect, either directly or by passing data via the app.
When Is the Best Time to Weigh Yourself?
Most experts say that the best time to weigh in is first thing in the morning, before you’ve eaten and after you’ve used the restroom. The main reason for this is consistency: Weighing yourself at the same time every day is the best way to ensure that consecutive weigh-ins are taken under conditions that are as controlled as possible. Since eating and drinking will cause your weight to fluctuate considerably, weighing yourself on an empty stomach means you’re getting an apples-to-apples comparison each morning.
As a small bonus, your weight is usually at its lowest right after you wake up, so you potentially stand to give yourself a gentle confidence boost by stepping on the scale then instead of after dinner.
Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
Other Smart Scales
Renpho MorphoScan for $170: The Renpho MorphoScan full-body scanner looks surprisingly similar to the Runstar FG2015, including a near-identical display attached to the handlebars. Well, spoiler alert: They are basically the same scale. They even use the same app to collect data (you can use both scales simultaneously with the app).
Runstar Smart Body Fat Scale (FG2015) for $140: My former pick for best full-body scanner, this admittedly garish offering tracks 20 metrics and supports 24 users, effectively breaking down information, limb-by-limb, in its Starfit mobile app. USB-C rechargeability is a nice plus, but the price tag—just $140 if you buy it directly from Runstar—is probably its best feature.
Tanita RD-953 InnerScan Pro for $230: One of the few new feet-only smart scales to hit the market this decade, Tanita’s RD-953 is defined by its Cylonesque looks—and its relative simplicity. The costly Bluetooth-only scale scans quickly, though the placement of its display in the center of the scale, right between your feet, can be awkward for those with even a small breadbasket between their head and the floor. I also didn’t love the very high and hopefully overstated body fat reading the scale gave me, but my harshest criticism is directed at the Healthy Edge app (a different app than is used by Tanita’s other scale), which is about as engaging and motivational as a shopping list on a Post-It Note.
Withings BodyFit for $230: The middle child in the Withings family sits comfortably between the no-holds-barred BodyScan 2 and the feet-only Body Comp Smart Scale, offering a pleasant alternative for users who want full-body analysis but don’t need (or want to pay for) the fitness extremism of Withings’s top-tier model. It’s a sleek and demure unit with a small but informative color screen, quick Wi-Fi connectivity, and fast performance—and, of course, it works seamlessly with Withings’s excellent app.
Arboleaf Body Fat Scale CS20W for $50: This affordable Bluetooth scale isn’t the most eye-catching I’ve tested in light of its big silver electrodes and an oversized display that comes across as a bit garish. While weight is easy to make out, the six additional statistics showcased are difficult to read, all displayed simultaneously. I like the Arboleaf app better than the scale, where five additional metrics are available, each featuring a helpful explanation when tapped. It’s a solid deal at this price, but the upsell to get an “intelligent interpretation report” for an extra $40 per year is probably safe to skip.
Hume Health Body Pod for $229: Hume Health’s Body Pod, another full-body scanner with handles, is heavily advertised—at least to the apps on my phone—and touted (by Hume) as the Next Big Thing in the world of body management. While the app is indeed glossy and inviting, I was shocked to discover how flimsy the hardware felt, that it lacked Wi-Fi, and that some features are locked behind a $100-a-year Hume Plus subscription plan. It works fine enough, but you can get results that are just as good with a cheaper device.
Garmin Index S2 for $200: Five years after its release, the Index S2 is still Garmin’s current model, a surprise for a company otherwise obsessed with fitness. It’s still noteworthy for its lovely color display, which walks you through its six body metrics (for up to 16 users) with each weigh-in. The display also provides your weight trend over time in graphical form and can even display the weather. The scale connects directly to Wi-Fi and Garmin’s cloud-based storage system, so—unlike with Bluetooth-only scales—you don’t need a phone nearby to track your progress. A phone running the Garmin Connect app (Android, iOS) is handy, so you can keep track of everything over time. Unfortunately, as health apps go, Connect is a bit of a bear, so expect a learning curve—especially if you want to make changes to the way the scale works. You can turn its various LCD-screen widgets on or off in the app, but finding everything can be difficult due to the daunting scope of the Garmin ecosystem. The color screen is nice at first, but it ultimately adds little to the package.
Omron BCM-500 for $85: With its large LCD panel, quartet of onboard buttons, and oversize silver electrodes, the Omron BCM-500 is an eye-catching masterwork of brutalist design. If your bathroom is decked out in concrete and wrought iron, this scale will fit right in. The Bluetooth unit syncs with Omron’s HeartAdvisor app (Android, iOS), but it provides all six of its body metrics directly on the scale, cycling through them with each weigh-in (for up to four users). It can be difficult to read the label for each of the data points, in part because the LCD isn’t backlit, but the app is somewhat easier to follow, offering front-page graphs of weight, skeletal muscle, and body fat. On the other hand, the presentation is rather clinical, and the app is surprisingly slow to sync. For a scale without a Wi-Fi connection, it’s also rather expensive.
Smart Scales to Avoid
Renpho MorphoScan Lite for $95: This new entry-level offering in the MorphoScan line is specifically designed for new GLP-1 users. It's a simpler device, ditching the handheld display and, critically, Wi-Fi connectivity. It’s also one of the flimsiest scales I’ve tested—too lightweight for you to extend the handlebars without inadvertently dragging the scale across the floor. If this were a mega-bargain in line with foot-only scale pricing, I’d be sold, but the meager savings compared to other MorphoScan scales don’t justify considering it.
Tanita RD-545 InnerScan Pro for $480: This monstrous, industrial scale looks more like it belongs in the mailroom than the bathroom, and its level of complexity only provides more supportive evidence. The Bluetooth-only scale is confusing to set up and difficult to use correctly, and I was only able to get successful measurements by first opening the mobile app and ensuring the scale was connected before carefully stepping onto it. Then, I had to wait for a prompt to pick up the handles (while balanced on the device). Testing feels like it takes forever, and that’s even if you get it right the first time. For $480, the scale is a questionable value at best, despite its 40 measurements offered. No Wi-Fi at this price, really?

Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.
Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.
Walter Benitez (Crystal Palace): His save from Liam Delap's effort, when Delap smashed the ball into his face, is the turning point of why Palace ended up winning that game. If that goes in, it is simply game over.
Ferdi Kadioglu (Brighton): He makes a massive block in the second half, which would have made it 1-1, and if the floodgates open it would be a problem. He is not known for his defensive skills, but he was great.
Jefferson Lerma (Crystal Palace): A centre-midfielder playing at centre-back. He scored a goal, made some big tackles, and was also was able to play out from the back, being the catalyst for Palace, so he goes in as well.
James Justin (Leeds): I know he loves playing against Arsenal, but the transformation he has had from when he was at Leicester to Leeds - the ability to play right wing-back, right centre-back. Everything that he gives you in that situation, he's just a joke of a centre-back. I don't believe he gets anywhere near enough credit. An unbelievable goal and he could have had more on the day.
Ethan Pinnock (Coventry): When he moved to Coventry from Brentford, I thought, that's a dodgy one for Coventry. He is decent, but he doesn't move the needle. How wrong was I? He has been excellent. A big physical presence, but also has that calming influence to talk others through games, and you can see since he's been in the team, Coventry have got better week-on-week.
Riccardo Calafiori (Arsenal): He's probably Arsenal's best forward at the moment. Getting in really good positions, defensively solid, but also offers you a lot from assists and goals.
Jordan Henderson (Chelsea): Two goals from the old boy. Thankfully he didn't climb over any of the hoardings and hurt himself. The confidence to say to Cole Palmer 'I know you just had an eight-year contract extension, but let me just put this in the top corner', and then he scores that free-kick.
Matt Grimes (Coventry): One of the unsung heroes. He moves the ball around really well, which he has been doing in the Championship for years. Me and a few others questioned whether he could make the step up, but I think against Newcastle he proved that he can.
Rayan Cherki (Manchester City): He's just the best football player to watch in world football, isn't he? He is the perfect player for City in this situation. Everybody hates them, everyone thinks that they cheated and he just walks on the pitch and says, 'give me the ball lads, let me have some fun'. He makes you smile while watching him.
Joao Pedro (Chelsea): He's going to have the season of his life with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer playing just behind him. He's just going to score.
Jeremy Doku (Manchester City): He changed the game with a goal and assist, all after he got Ryan Gravenberch sent off. If he can play like that between now and the end of the season, then City will probably win the league and go deep in the Champions League.
Enzo Maresca (Manchester City): Got the job done at Anfield, but also galvanised the team and made it all about 'us versus the rest of the world'. The one thing he hasn't got credit for is his tactical change of bringing on Doku, who changed the game. It all comes down to Maresca. Top of the league and just rolling away at the moment.

Quick Answer
Turn rough screen recordings into polished demos with tools that auto-zoom on clicks, follow and smooth the cursor, add clean framing, and highlight key actions. Options include Screen Studio, FocuSee, Screen Awesome, and ScreenCursor.
When you record a two-minute walkthrough of your app, for instance, a setting buried five menus deep, or a spreadsheet trick you are proud of, there is something that can leave you frustrated. You press play, and the cursor is dancing all around without highlighting what you actually wanted to show. Either the text is too small to read on a phone or the whole thing looks like security-camera footage of your desktop. The old-school way is to use a video editor, add zooms by hand, pan the camera to follow your cursor, and nudge keyframes for an hour. Thankfully, there is a newer batch of screen recorders that automatically do that part for you.
In this guide, we have covered four of them. They not only differ in price, platform, and functionality, but each one also has one detail that surprised me.
|  | Screen Studio | FocuSee | Screen Awesome | ScreenCursor | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Works on | Mac only | Windows and Mac | Chrome (also Edge, Brave and similar) | Chrome (Mac, Windows, Linux) | 
| Price | $9/mo billed yearly, or $29/mo | Free trial, paid plans | Free | $49 one-time (early pricing) | 
| Best for | Maximum polish on a Mac | All-in-one AI extras | Privacy and zero cost | Pay-once simplicity | 
Table of Contents
Why do raw screen recordings look so rough?
When you use any standard screen recorder, like the one built into your OS, it captures pixels and nothing else. It has no idea what mattered. It doesn’t know if you clicked a tiny button that you want the viewers to look at. The result? You get a full-screen recording of everything, including your cursor wandering here and there. Viewers watch these videos on laptops and phones, and since the important part is not zoomed in or clearly shown, they will miss it. A better screen recording would be one where:
- Zoom is on the action so people can actually read what you click.
- A camera that follows your cursor instead of leaving viewers guessing.
- A cursor that glides rather than jitters.
- A clean frame, such as a gradient background and rounded corners.
With all of the above, your screen recording not only looks professional but also provides clear instructions for viewers.
Screen recorders with auto cursor follow and zoom
Here are some of the best screen recorders that you can use for automatic cursor follow and zoom.
Screen Studio: The one the others get compared to
If you are on Mac, then Screen Studio is one of the best options for screen recording with automatic cursor follow and zoom. When you’re recording using Screen Studio, it looks at what you did, like where you clicked, and zooms in on the moments that matter. Every zoom is balanced and animated automatically; you don’t have to worry about handling them. The best part is that you can choose between two styles: Classic zoom is the one you usually see in polished product videos. Then there is Loupe zoom, which is a magnifier-style alternative. If you want to zoom somewhere the app did not automatically add one, you can drop it onto the timeline and point it where you like. Notably, the cursor gets the same treatment. Shaky movement is smoothed out into a steady glide, and clicks get a soft ripple. Fast movements pick up motion blur so they look filmed rather than captured. You also have the option to change the cursor’s size and style later. Some of the notable features of Screen Studio are:
- Edit by transcript: Delete a sentence from the transcript, and it disappears from the video. Filler words and long pauses can be cleared in one pass.
- One recording, many shapes: Record once, then switch the aspect ratio between wide (16:9), square (1:1), and vertical (9:16). Zooms can be re-aimed, layouts rearranged, and captions moved to stay readable. You can also choose the “Reel mode” that shows where Instagram’s or TikTok’s interface would cover your video, so you’re in the grey area where your inputs get hidden.
- Hide the private stuff: If the recording shows an API key or email address, you can mask it after the recording is complete, and the mask blends into the interface around it.
- iPhone and iPad framing: Plug your iPhone or iPad into a USB cable, pick the device, and record. Screen Studio wraps the footage in a matching device frame.
FocuSee: The Windows-friendly all-rounder
FocuSee comes from the house of iMobie and is a screen recording tool that works on both Windows and Mac. This already makes it the practical choice for many people working on either OS. FocuSee’s auto zoom follows your clicks and even your typing. This tool adds a spotlight to highlight areas worth noticing, making it much easier for anyone following your instructions. You can also choose a “3D Motion” mode that adds tilt and perspective that follows your cursor, for a more cinematic look. The cursor can fade out when you are not actively using it or don’t need it and reappears when you do. Similar to other screen recording tools, you can swap the cursor style and click animations. There are a bunch of features that deserve to be highlighted.
- A built-in teleprompter: You can show your script on screen while recording with the option to adjust the font size, speed, and position. If you tend to forget the script midway, this alone might sell you.
- An annotation suite: You can add text, shapes, arrows, callouts, spotlights, and blur effects. Moreover, you can stack several layers to walk viewers through a tricky step, or blur out something sensitive.
- An AI avatar: This one is for those who are camera-shy or do not want their face in the video. FocuSee can create a digital presenter, or in simple words, an AI avatar. It is a niche feature, but a handy one for company tutorials.
- Smart cleanup: You can remove filler words and silence with just one click, and also enhance voice and reduce noise with just a button.
- Background fixes for your webcam: It can blur or replace a messy room behind you after recording without needing a green screen.
- Add Subtitles: FocuSee supports speech recognition in over 50 languages, with accuracy above 98%. You can add your own subtitles and make it easier for the follower to go through the steps.
Screen Awesome: Free, and it can’t upload your recordings
Screen Awesome is a different kind of tool. It’s actually a free Chrome extension built by a developer named Nitinbhai Viras. On one hand, most apps say “we respect your privacy” and simply ask you to take their word; Screen Awesome does things a bit differently. Screen Awesome points you at Chrome’s own permission screen and requests no access to any website. It is not allowed to contact any server. That means it cannot upload your recordings, even if it wanted to. The best part is that you can verify this yourself in about 30 seconds. Head over to chrome://extensions, find Screen Awesome, click Details, and look at the Site access line. According to the developer, it reads none. On the extension’s settings page, there is a button that jumps you straight there. On top of this security, you get this tool for absolutely free. Here are some features that set Screen Awesome apart:
- Auto-zoom to clicks: While recording a browser tab, Screen Awesome notes where you click. A virtual camera follows each click and pans between them. You have the option to preview it, turn it off, or export the file. This works for tab recording.
- Serious annotation tools: Arrows, pen, highlighter, shapes, text, speech bubbles, step counters, emoji stamps, and a blur that destroys the pixels rather than just smudging them. You can edit all of these marks.
- Product-shot framing: You can place a recording on a backdrop with rounded corners, a soft shadow, and an optional browser window around it, and also change its aspect ratio to 16:9, etc.
- Formats: You can export your recording in MP4, WebM, or an animated GIF.
- Webcam and voice: Screen Awesome lets you mix in your microphone and the tab’s audio, and even add a movable webcam bubble while recording if you want to show your face.
ScreenCursor: Pay once, and record in Chrome
ScreenCursor is another screen recording tool that works as a Chrome extension. However, its approach is the opposite of Screen Awesome’s. Notably, it does one thing and tries to do it well, which is turning clicks into camera moves with as little fuss as possible. When you hit the record button, ScreenCursor waits three seconds before it starts. That gap is deliberate, and it exists because Chrome shows its own “sharing your screen” bar while recording, and unfortunately it cannot be switched off. With this delay, you get the time to collapse the bar before the screen recording starts. Every click, drag, and keystroke gets zoomed in. Each zoom happens a beat before the action; this way, viewers are already looking at the right spot, then the camera holds steady and follows your cursor. ScreenCursor gives you the option to manually retime a zoom, push its depth in or out, switch the motion between snappy and gentle, or delete the zoom you don’t want. Here are some of the highlights of ScreenCursor:
- Zoom focus point: Right-click any zoom, drag a box over the part you want people to see, and the zoom shows exactly that. You can use this on recordings of desktop apps, since ScreenCursor can record your whole screen.
- Customization: You also get wallpapers, gradients, or use your own image as a backdrop. There is a browser frame that carries the real page title. Editing is also possible, as you can split the clip, delete boring stretches, and speed up slow ones.
- Price and limits: It costs $49 once, which is labeled “early pricing,” with $79 shown as the regular price. After one-time payment, you will continue to receive updates and can work on up to three of your own computers.

Kelly made these remarks during the Oct. 5 episode of "The Megyn Kelly Show." She called her thoughts "the narrative that is likely to have occurred here, in my opinion." She did not identify Jane Doe by name, nor did she provide any evidence credibly confirming the woman's identity.
Last week, Snopes readers searched our site and sent us emails asking whether political podcaster and former Fox News host Megyn Kelly made remarks critical of the Jane Doe in the Cornell University rape case.
That Jane Doe, a former female Cornell student not identified by name in court documents or elsewhere to protect her identity, has accused seven current or former male Cornell students of sexually assaulting and raping her in an on-campus fraternity house between Oct. 19 and 20, 2024. Snopes has produced numerous reports examining claims regarding the case.
In this instance, one reader sent an image purportedly showing a text transcript of Kelly's comments, asking, "Did Megyn Kelly say [this] on Oct. 5?" Another reader asked whether someone created video of the remarks with an artificial intelligence tool. The email read, in part:
I saw a horrific video of Megyn Kelly victim blaming Jane Doe who has accused seven Cornell University fraternity members of raping her. It was so offensive I was in disbelief that even Megan Kelly would stoop so low.
And it wasn't just me, because others in the thread following the post also wondered if what we saw was real or AI.
The text transcript image, or quotes from it, also appeared on Facebook, Instagram, Threads and X.
(@girlsreallyrule via X)
According to the transcript users shared, Kelly said she believes Jane Doe "made a decision to get it on" with four of the seven accused male students and "enjoyed it," and made negative remarks about the alleged Jane Doe's physical appearance.
In sum, Kelly authentically made these statements during Monday's episode of "The Megyn Kelly Show." SiriusXM and YouTube broadcast the show live. The relevant moments begin at around the 15-minute mark in this YouTube video.
During the episode, Kelly does not identify Jane Doe by name, nor does she provide any evidence credibly confirming the woman's identity.
Snopes contacted Kelly's Devil May Care Media company to ask if she wished to provide further comment, seeing as users were sharing her words and questioning whether she actually made the remarks. We will update this article if we receive further details.
More of what Kelly said
Just before the transcript shared on social media begins, Kelly says, "How is this progress? The absolute freak-out by all women. Not all of them are freaking out, but the ones who are, over this, accounts for zero agency for women whatsoever."
The transcript begins immediately after that, with Kelly saying, "No one will even consider the possibility that this woman made a decision to get it on with four men total, not seven, and enjoyed it because, I'm just going to be honest, she's not the most attractive gal." She then criticizes the physical appearance of the woman she asserts is Jane Doe.
Kelly describes her thoughts as "the narrative that is likely to have occurred here, in my opinion."
Her mention of "four men total, not seven" referenced reporting appearing to come from The New York Times, saying that only four of the accused men acknowledged having sexual contact with Jane Doe. The Times reported:
But in hours of interviews and a statement collected during Cornell's administrative investigation over the winter of 2024, all the men denied any wrongdoing. Four acknowledged having sexual contact with the woman but said that their interactions had been consensual. The others denied participating in sexual encounters.
